s: A Tesla driver using Autopilot hit a motorcycle from behind on a Utah interstate at night, killing the motorcyclist. The driver said they did not see the rider, and federal regulators investigated.

t: Grab Tweaked Matchmaking Algorithm, Providing Preferential Treatment to Drivers Registered with Affiliated Car Rental Service
s: Indonesia's competition regulator fined Grab for favoring drivers renting cars through an affiliated company, including by tweaking its ride-matching algorithm to give them more rides than other drivers.

t: FaceApp Predicted Different Genders for Similar User Photos with Slight Variations
s: A user reported that FaceApp labeled two otherwise identical selfies as different genders depending on whether eyebrows looked thick or thin. The user described the inconsistency as distressing and changed their appearance to avoid it.

t: Virginia Courts’ Algorithmic Recidivism Risk Assessment Failed to Lower Incarceration Rates
s: Researchers studying Virginia's use of algorithmic risk scores in felony sentencing found no overall reduction in incarceration and no public-safety benefit. Judges applied scores unevenly by race, and young defendants received relatively longer sentences.

t: Facebook’s Moderation Algorithm Banned Users for Historical Evidence of Slavery
s: Facebook's automated moderation removed posts and restricted users who shared an article containing an 1890s photograph of Aboriginal men in chains, wrongly flagging it as nudity. Facebook later apologized and called it an error.

t: Local South Korean Government’s Use of CCTV Footage Analysis via Facial Recognition to Track COVID Cases Raised Concerns about Privacy, Retention, and Potential Misuse
s: A South Korean city piloted AI facial recognition on thousands of CCTV cameras to trace COVID-19 cases. Privacy advocates and some lawmakers objected over consent and possible data misuse.

t: Voices Created Using Publicly Available App Stolen and Resold as NFT without Attribution
s: An NFT company used a synthetic voice from a free text-to-speech web app in a promotional animation without crediting it. The company later admitted the voice was taken from the app and apologized.

t: Meta’s BlenderBot 3 Chatbot Demo Made Offensive Antisemitic Comments
s: Meta's public BlenderBot 3 chatbot demo produced antisemitic tropes and election-denial claims within days of launch, and also claimed to be a Christian and a plumber. Meta acknowledged it could make offensive remarks.

t: TikTok’s “For You” Algorithm Exposed Young Users to Pro-Eating Disorder Content
s: TikTok's personalized For You feed was reported to serve pro-eating-disorder content to young users, despite the platform's own rules. Later research found teen accounts received self-harm and eating disorder videos within minutes.

t: Coffee Meets Bagel’s Algorithm Reported by Users Disproportionately Showing Them Matches of Their Own Ethnicities Despite Selecting “No Preference”
s: Users of the dating app Coffee Meets Bagel who chose 'no preference' on ethnicity were shown mostly matches of their own ethnicity or one group. The founder said the algorithm uses data on past behavior to maximize connection.

t: YouTube's Algorithms Failed to Remove Violating Content Related to Suicide and Self-Harm
s: Videos with graphic self-harm content stayed on YouTube despite its policies, and were reportedly recommended to users as young as 13. YouTube removed some flagged videos and search suggestions after being notified.

t: Facebook’s Algorithm Mistook an Advertisement of Onions as Sexual Suggestive Content
s: Facebook's automated moderation removed a Canadian garden center's ad for onion seeds, flagging a photo of onions as sexually suggestive. Facebook restored the ad after review and apologized.

t: Facebook’s Automated Content Moderation Tool Flagged a Post Containing Parts of the Declaration of Independence as Hate Speech by Mistake
s: Facebook's automated hate-speech detection removed a small Texas newspaper's post quoting the Declaration of Independence. Facebook said it was a mistake, restored the post and apologized.

t: Facebook’s Automated Removal of Content Featuring Nudity-Containing Artworks Denounced as Censorship
s: Facebook removed posts and ads featuring famous historical artworks because of nudity, drawing complaints of cultural censorship from museums and tourism boards.

t: Google Lens’s Camera-Based Translation Feature Provided an Offensive Mistranslation of a Book Title in Korean
s: Google Lens's camera translation reportedly rendered the title of a book by Korea's first culture minister as an offensive phrase in English.

t: TikTok’s "For You" Allegedly Pushed Fatal “Blackout” Challenge Videos to Two Young Girls
s: Parents of two girls aged 8 and 9 sued TikTok, alleging its 'For You' algorithm pushed 'blackout challenge' videos to their children before they died. TikTok said the challenge predates its platform and was never a TikTok trend.

t: OpenAI’s GPT-3 Reported as Unviable in Medical Tasks by Healthcare Firm
s: A French digital health company tested GPT-3 for medical documentation, diagnosis support and treatment advice. It found the model too inconsistent and lacking medical expertise to be safe for healthcare use.

t: New Jersey Police Wrongful Arrested Innocent Black Man via FRT
s: Police in Woodbridge, New Jersey, arrested a Black man after facial recognition software wrongly matched him to a shoplifting suspect. He spent 10 days in jail and about $5,000 on his defense before charges were dismissed.

t: Starship Delivery Robot Scuffed Bumper of a Resident’s Car in Texas, Allegedly Refusing to Release Footage of the Accident
s: A Starship delivery robot crossing a street in Frisco, Texas, hit a waiting car and caused over $2,600 in bumper damage. The company reportedly did not provide the driver with its footage, and it later agreed to pay.

t: False Negatives for Water Quality-Associated Beach Closures
s: Toronto used an AI model to predict beach water quality at two beaches. A water advocacy group and later analysis found it often marked contaminated water as safe, so beaches stayed open on unsafe days.

t: Tesla Allegedly Misled Customers about Autopilot and FSD Capabilities
s: California's motor vehicle regulator accused Tesla of false advertising, saying the names and descriptions of Autopilot and Full Self-Driving made the driver-assist features sound more capable than they are.

t: Apple’s AVs Reportedly Struggled to Navigate Streets in Silicon Valley Test Drives
s: Apple's prototype self-driving cars reportedly hit curbs and drifted out of lanes on test drives near its headquarters. One car reportedly nearly hit a jogger who had the right of way.

t: Cruise’s Self-Driving Car Involved in a Multiple-Injury Collision at an San Francisco Intersection
s: A driverless Cruise vehicle in San Francisco made a left turn in front of an oncoming Toyota Prius, and people in both cars were injured. The company says its vehicle had stopped and the other driver was speeding.

t: Tesla Autopilot Allegedly Malfunctioned in a Non-Fatal Collision in Greece
s: A Tesla Model 3 driver in Greece said Autopilot suddenly veered right at a highway fork and hit a barrier. He was unhurt, and Tesla said the driver must stay responsible for the car.

t: Wrongful Attempted Arrest for Apple Store Thefts Due to NYPD’s Facial Misidentification
s: A Black teenager in New York was wrongly linked to a series of Apple Store thefts and faced arrest and charges in several states. His lawsuit says a facial recognition system and mixed-up identification records tied his identity to the real thief's face.

t: Twitter Recommender System Amplified Right-Leaning Tweets
s: Twitter's own researchers found its algorithmic Home timeline amplified tweets from right-leaning politicians and news outlets more than left-leaning ones in six of seven countries studied. Twitter said the cause was unclear.

t: EasyMile Self-Driving Shuttle Unexpectedly Stopped Mid-Route, Injuring a Passenger
s: A self-driving shuttle in Columbus, Ohio stopped suddenly mid-route and a passenger fell from her seat, suffering minor injuries. The city paused the service and federal regulators restricted the manufacturer from carrying passengers.

t: Student-Developed Facial Recognition App Raised Ethical Concerns
s: A Harvard student built a campus social networking app using facial recognition, which raised concerns about privacy, security and misuse. The database later reclassified it as an issue rather than an incident.

t: Japanese Porn Depixelated by Man using Deepfake
s: Japanese police arrested a man who used AI to reconstruct the pixelated parts of adult videos and sold the results online, in the country's first criminal case involving AI-manipulated content. He pleaded guilty to copyright and obscenity charges.

t: TikTok's "For You" Algorithm Allegedly Abused by Online Personality to Promote Anti-Women Hate
s: Reporting found TikTok's For You feed pushed misogynistic videos by an online personality to young male users, helped by coordinated efforts to game the algorithm, despite platform rules banning such content.

t: Honorlock's AI Proctoring System Reportedly Led Broward College to Accuse a Teenager of Cheating
s: A remote proctoring system flagged a Florida community college student as suspicious during an exam, leading the college to accuse her of cheating. She said the accusation was unfounded, and the report describes it as a human judgment based on flagged footage.

t: Dartmouth's Geisel School of Medicine Reportedly Used Canvas Activity Logs to Accuse Students of Cheating
s: A medical school used learning-platform activity logs to accuse 17 students of cheating on remote exams. Outside experts said automated platform activity may have been misread as misconduct, and the charges were later dropped.

t: Google’s Automated Child Abuse Detection Wrongfully Flagged a Parent’s Naked Photo of His Child
s: Google's automated child-abuse image detection flagged medical photos a father took of his toddler for a doctor. He lost his accounts and was investigated by police, and appeals were rejected.

t: Tesla on FSD Reportedly Drove into the Wrong Lane in California
s: A Tesla Model Y using Full Self-Driving beta reportedly steered into the wrong lane during a left turn in Brea, California, and was hit by another vehicle. The owner said the car overrode his attempt to correct it. No one was injured.

t: YouTube’s Recommendation Algorithm Allegedly Promoted Climate Misinformation Content
s: An advocacy group alleged that YouTube's recommendation system steered millions of viewers toward climate misinformation videos. YouTube said it had invested in reducing recommendations of borderline content.

t: Tesla on Autopilot TACC Crashed into Van on European Highway
s: A Tesla Model S using Autopilot's cruise control crashed into a stopped van on a European highway. The driver said he trusted the system, and the front of the car was heavily damaged.

t: iPhone Face ID Failed to Recognize Users’ Morning Faces
s: Some iPhone X owners reported that Face ID often failed to recognize their faces in the first part of the morning, forcing them to use a passcode. The effect appeared to fade within about half an hour.

t: Atlas Robot Fell off Stage at Conference
s: Boston Dynamics' humanoid robot Atlas fell off a stage during a public demonstration after reportedly catching its foot on a stage light.

t: Facial Recognition Trial Performed Poorly at Notting Hill Carnival
s: London police trialled live facial recognition at the 2017 Notting Hill Carnival. Of 96 people the system flagged, only one was a correct match, and that person was no longer wanted. Several people were stopped and questioned before being released.

t: High False Positive Rate by SWP's Facial Recognition Use at Champion's League Final
s: South Wales Police used automated facial recognition at the 2017 Champions League final in Cardiff, and about 92% of its matches were wrong. Police said no one was wrongly arrested.

t: YouTube Auto-Moderation Reportedly Banned Women of Sex Tech Conference
s: YouTube's automated moderation removed the live stream of a women's sex tech conference and banned it from the platform though it broke no policies. YouTube blamed greater reliance on automation during the pandemic.

t: Startup's Accent Translation AI Denounced as Reinforcing Racial Bias
s: A startup's AI that removes or changes call center workers' accents drew criticism that it reinforces racial bias by making voices sound white and American. The company denies this.

t: BlenderBot 3 Cited Dutch Politician as a Terrorist
s: Meta's research chatbot BlenderBot 3, asked who is a terrorist, falsely named a prominent Dutch politician. She said the claim was untrue and worried about people with less power to correct such errors.

t: Stable Diffusion Abused by 4chan Users to Deepfake Celebrity Porn
s: Stability AI's open-source Stable Diffusion image generator leaked early on 4chan, where users shared AI-generated nude images of celebrities and other pornography.

t: Facial Recognition Service Abused to Target Russian Porn Actresses
s: A face-matching service that links photos to social media profiles was used by online forum members to identify and harass Russian women who appeared in pornography or were alleged sex workers, including by messaging their families and friends.

t: Facebook Ad-Approval Algorithm Allegedly Missed Fraudulent Ads via Simple URL Checks
s: A security analyst reported that Facebook's ad-approval system failed to catch ads whose displayed domain differed from where they led, letting scam ads for supplements reach users while impersonating reputable news sites.

t: Bug in Facebook’s Anti-Spam Filter Allegedly Blocked Legitimate Posts about COVID-19
s: In March 2020 Facebook wrongly blocked users from posting legitimate news articles about the coronavirus, which its spam filter flagged. Facebook said it was a bug unrelated to moderator staffing changes and began restoring the posts.

t: Facebook Recommended Military Gear Ads Despite Pause on Weapons Accessories Ads
s: After Facebook paused ads for gun accessories and military gear following the Capitol attack, researchers found such ads still appearing next to extremist and insurrection posts in the feeds of monitoring accounts.

t: Tesla on Autopilot Fatally Crashed into Parked Fire Truck in Indiana
s: A Tesla rear-ended a parked fire truck on an Indiana interstate, killing the passenger and seriously injuring the driver. Federal regulators later said the car was on Autopilot and opened a broader investigation of similar crashes.

t: Tesla on Autopilot Collided with Parked Fire Truck on California Freeway
s: A Tesla Model S being driven with Autopilot engaged crashed into the back of a parked fire truck on a Culver City freeway. No one was hurt. Investigators cited the driver's inattention and the system allowing him to disengage from driving.

t: Tesla Model X on Autopilot Crashed into California Highway Barrier, Killing Driver
s: A Tesla Model X with Autopilot engaged hit a concrete highway divider in Mountain View, California, and caught fire, killing the driver. Tesla said the driver's hands were not detected on the wheel in the seconds before the crash.

t: Tesla Model 3 Crashed into Police Patrol Car on Connecticut Highway
s: A Tesla Model 3 using Autopilot hit a parked police car on a Connecticut interstate, then struck a disabled vehicle. The driver admitted he was not watching the road. No one was seriously injured.

t: Tesla on Autopilot Crashed into Parked Police Car in California
s: A Tesla using Autopilot crashed into a parked police car in Laguna Beach, California. The driver had minor injuries and the officer was not in the vehicle, which was totaled.

t: GAN Faces Deployed by The BL's Fake Account Network to Push Pro-Trump Content on Meta Platforms
s: Facebook removed a network of more than 900 accounts, pages and groups tied to a media outlet called The BL that used AI-generated profile photos to make fake accounts look real while pushing pro-Trump content to millions of users.

t: Offensive Instagram User Content Displayed as Facebook Ad
s: Instagram used a user's post containing a violent rape threat, which she had shared to highlight online abuse, as an advertisement to her friends and family on Facebook.

t: Facebook Automated Year-in-Review Highlights Showed Users Painful Memories
s: Facebook's automated Year in Review feature showed some users painful memories, such as a photo of a child who had died, under a cheerful banner. Facebook apologised and changed the wording.

t: Facebook’s On-This-Day Feature Mistakenly Showed Painful Memories to Users
s: Facebook's On This Day feature resurfaced painful past posts, such as a memorial for a friend who died by suicide, which upset users. The company said it had added precautions after earlier similar mistakes.

t: Fake Accounts Using GAN Faces Deployed by Propaganda Campaign on Social Platforms
s: A pro-China propaganda network used AI-generated profile photos for fake accounts on Facebook, Twitter and YouTube to boost videos critical of the US. The campaign was clumsy and drew little genuine engagement.

t: Amazon Reportedly Recommends Explosive-Producing Ingredients as 'Frequently Bought Together' Items for Chemicals
s: A news investigation found that Amazon's automated 'frequently bought together' suggestions grouped chemicals that can be combined into explosives and incendiary devices, along with related components. The test purchase was not completed.

t: “Amazon’s Choice” Algorithm Failed to Recommend Functional Products and Prone to Review Manipulation
s: Amazon's Choice badge, which recommends products partly by star ratings, was shown on products with faulty quality and with recycled or purchased reviews. Amazon was reported as unable to stop the review manipulation.

t: Bug in Instagram’s “Related Hashtags” Algorithm Allegedly Caused Disproportionate Treatment of Political Hashtags
s: Instagram acknowledged a bug that stopped related hashtags from appearing for thousands of hashtags. The effect reportedly shielded major Trump campaign hashtags from negative associations while Biden hashtags showed smears.

t: Google Images Showed Racially Biased Results for 'Professional' Hairstyles
s: Google Images searches for 'professional hairstyles' returned mostly white women, while 'unprofessional hairstyles' returned mostly Black women. The results prompted public outrage over racial bias.

t: Tesla on Autopilot Crashed Parked Michigan Police Car on Interstate
s: A Tesla Model Y that its driver said was using Autopilot hit a parked Michigan State Police car that had its emergency lights on. No one was injured, and federal regulators opened an investigation.

t: Uber Deployed Secret Program To Deny Local Authorities Rides
s: Uber used a secret tool called Greyball that used data such as location and payment information to identify suspected city officials and show them a fake version of its app, so officials running stings could not get rides.

t: UK Visa Streamline Algorithm Allegedly Discriminated Based on Nationality
s: Campaigners challenged a UK Home Office algorithm that sorted visa applications into green, yellow and red channels using nationality, arguing it discriminated by race. The Home Office denied bias but suspended the tool and committed to a redesign.

t: UK Home Office's Sham Marriage Detection Algorithm Reportedly Flagged Certain Nationalities Disproportionately
s: A UK Home Office algorithm triages marriages for sham-marriage investigation. Campaigners say it rates couples of some nationalities red far more often, uses factors like age gap, and its criteria are kept secret.

t: Tesla Model S on ACC Crashed into Tree in Texas, Killing Two People
s: A Tesla Model S crashed into a tree in Texas and caught fire, killing two men. Investigators found no one in the driver's seat, while Tesla said driver-assist features were limited and disputed the account.

t: Students Reportedly Used Generative Text Tools to Complete School Assignments and Exams
s: Students reportedly used generative text tools such as Sudowrite, GPT-3 and ChatGPT to complete essays and assignments without disclosure, prompting educators to call for policies and controls against cheating.

t: Honda's CMBS False Positives Allegedly Caused Accidents to Customers
s: Drivers alleged that Honda's Collision Mitigation Braking System braked suddenly for obstacles that were not there, causing accidents, injuries and property damage. A class action lawsuit was pending.

t: Nissan's "Automatic Emergency Braking" False Positives Posed Traffic Risks to Drivers
s: Owners and a class-action lawsuit say Nissan's automatic emergency braking sometimes brakes hard for obstacles that are not there, even in intersections. Complaints reported crashes and injuries, and the company has not issued a recall.

t: Facebook, Instagram, and Twitter Failed to Proactively Remove Targeted Racist Remarks via Automated Systems
s: After England lost the Euro 2020 final, trolls posted racist comments and emojis at three Black players on Facebook, Instagram and Twitter. The platforms did not proactively catch many of them and relied on user reports.

t: Hiring Algorithms Provided Invalid Positive Results for Interview Responses in German
s: MIT Technology Review tested two AI job-interview tools and found they gave positive scores, including English competency ratings, to a candidate who answered in German by reading an encyclopedia entry.

t: Auto-Insurance Photo-Based Estimation Allegedly Gave Inaccurate Repair Prices Frequently
s: Auto repair shop owners and industry groups alleged that insurers' photo-based and AI repair estimates were often inaccurate, leaving damaged cars in shops longer.

t: Robots in Japanese Hotel Annoyed Guests and Failed to Handle Simple Tasks
s: A Japanese hotel staffed largely by robots laid off about half of them after guests complained the machines were annoying and could not handle simple tasks such as answering questions or copying passports.

t: Waymo Self-Driving Taxi Reportedly Behaved Unexpectedly, Driving away from Support Crew
s: A Waymo driverless taxi in Arizona became confused by road cones, blocked traffic, and twice drove away from a roadside assistance worker with a passenger aboard before a human took over.

t: YouTube Recommendation Reportedly Pushed Election Fraud Content to Skeptics Disproportionately
s: A New York University study found YouTube's recommendations pushed about three times as many election-fraud videos to users most skeptical of the 2020 election as to the least skeptical. YouTube disputed that the study reflects how its systems work.

t: Evolv AI Weapons Detection System Allegedly Misrepresents Accuracy, Leading to School Security Gaps
s: Evolv's AI weapons scanners, sold to schools as better than metal detectors, reportedly missed weapons and raised many false alarms. The FTC alleged deceptive claims, and in one case a missed knife was used to stab a student.

t: Delivery Robot Rolled Through Crime Scene
s: A sidewalk delivery robot in Los Angeles rolled through police caution tape at a crime scene, and the video went viral. The company said a remote human operator, not the robot's software, chose to proceed.

t: "The Little Mermaid" Clip Doctored Using Generative AI to Replace Black Actress with White Character
s: A social media user used generative AI to alter a clip from a Disney film trailer, replacing the Black lead actress with a white digital character. Critics called it racist and the accounts involved were suspended.

t: GPT-3-Based Twitter Bot Hijacked Using Prompt Injection Attacks
s: Twitter users hijacked a GPT-3-powered remote-jobs bot by telling it to ignore its instructions, making it repeat embarrassing phrases. The operator shut the bot down after the exploit went viral.

t: Tesla on Autopilot Crashed into Trailer Truck in Florida, Killing Driver
s: A Tesla Model 3 driver switched on Autopilot about ten seconds before the car drove under a tractor-trailer crossing a Florida highway, killing him. Investigators found he probably did not see the truck and the driver-assistance system apparently did not either.

t: Uber Allegedly Violated GDPR by Failing to Provide Sufficient Notice on Automated Profiling for Drivers
s: Uber drivers filed a legal action alleging Uber failed to give them their personal data and clear information about the automated decision-making and profiling applied to them, as required by European data protection law.

t: Uber Allegedly Wrongfully Accused Drivers of Fraud via Automated Systems
s: Uber drivers in the UK and Portugal were dismissed after Uber's systems flagged them for fraud. They say the accusations were false and that they were given no evidence and no right of appeal.

t: Philosophy AI Tentatively Produced Offensive Results for Certain Prompts
s: Users found that Philosopher AI, an app built on GPT-3, often produced offensive and racist text when prompted on topics such as feminism and Ethiopia, within a few attempts.

t: GPT-2 Reportedly Reproduced Personal Data from Its Training Data
s: Researchers showed that the GPT-2 language model memorized and could be prompted to reproduce personal information from its training data, such as names, phone numbers and email addresses. OpenAI later worked on a filter to block such outputs.

t: Calgary Malls Reportedly Deployed Facial Recognition Without Customer Consent
s: Shopping malls in Calgary used facial analysis software on directory cameras to estimate shoppers' ages and genders without notifying them or obtaining consent. The owner said no images were stored.

t: Facebook, Instagram, and Twitter Cited Errors in Automated Systems as Cause for Blocking pro-Palestinian Content on Israeli-Palestinian Conflict
s: During the May 2021 Israeli-Palestinian conflict, Facebook, Instagram and Twitter wrongly blocked or restricted many pro-Palestinian posts and accounts. The companies blamed errors in their automated systems and said they restored the accounts.

t: McDonald's AI Drive-Thru Allegedly Collected Biometric Customer Data without Consent, Violating BIPA
s: A customer sued McDonald's in Illinois, alleging its AI drive-thru voice ordering system collected customers' voiceprints without the written consent the state's biometric privacy law requires.

t: Amazon Echo Mistakenly Recorded and Sent Private Conversation to Random Contact
s: A Portland family said their Amazon Alexa speaker recorded a private conversation at home and sent the audio to one of the husband's employees. Amazon called it an extremely rare occurrence and said it was taking steps to prevent a repeat.

t: Facebook's Automated Moderation Flagged Gardening Group's Language Use by Mistake
s: Facebook's automated moderation flagged the word hoe in a gardening group as harassment, putting the group at risk of removal.

t: Facebook's Automated Moderation Mistakenly Flagged Landmark's Name as Offensive
s: Facebook's automated moderation wrongly treated posts mentioning Plymouth Hoe, a historic landmark, as using a misogynist term. Some users had comments removed or were temporarily restricted, and Facebook apologised.

t: Walmart's Bagging-Detection False Positives Exposed Workers to Health Risk
s: Walmart's AI self-checkout theft-detection system reportedly flagged legitimate scans as errors during the pandemic, prompting staff to step in close to shoppers and raising health concerns among employees.

t: Suicide Clips Evaded TikTok's Automated Moderation in Coordinated Attack
s: Clips of a man's suicide, first livestreamed elsewhere, spread across TikTok despite its automated moderation. TikTok said groups planned a coordinated effort to upload edited versions, and parents said their children were traumatised.

t: iGPT, SimCLR Learned Biased Associations from Internet Training Data
s: Researchers found that image-generation models iGPT and SimCLR, trained on unlabeled internet images, learned racial and gender stereotypes, such as completing cropped photos of women in revealing clothing.

t: Facial Recognition Smart Phone App 'Blue Wolf' Reportedly Monitored Palestinians in the West Bank
s: The Israeli military reportedly used a smartphone app called Blue Wolf and face-scanning cameras to photograph Palestinians in the West Bank, match them to a large database, and flag whether they should be detained or arrested. Soldiers reportedly competed to collect the most photos.

t: GAN Artwork Won First Place at State Fair Competition
s: An image made with the AI tool Midjourney won first place in the digital art category at the Colorado State Fair. Working artists objected, saying AI-generated work threatens creative jobs and makes competition unfair.

t: Google Fined for Changing Shopping Algorithms in EU to Favor Own Service
s: The EU fined Google 2.4 billion euros for favoring its own shopping comparison service over rivals in search results. An EU court later upheld the fine and rejected Google's argument that its algorithm changes improved search quality.

t: Uganda Deployed Huawei's Facial Recognition to Monitor Political Opposition and Protests
s: Uganda's government used a Huawei-supplied surveillance system with facial recognition to monitor opposition rallies and protests. Activists feared it would be used to suppress dissent, and police confirmed it helped track suspects after protests.

t: Users Reported Security Issues with Google Pixel 6a's Fingerprint Unlocking
s: Users reported that Google's Pixel 6a phone could be unlocked by fingerprints that had not been registered. A reviewer's friend unlocked the phone repeatedly, and video creators demonstrated the same problem. Google said the sensor met industry standards.

t: Michigan's Unemployment Benefits Algorithm MiDAS Issued False Fraud Claims to Thousands of People
s: Michigan's automated unemployment system wrongly accused thousands of people of fraud between 2013 and 2015. Many faced garnished wages, bankruptcy and other hardship, and a state review found most of the reviewed accusations were errors.

t: UK Ofqual's Algorithm Disproportionately Provided Lower Grades Than Teachers' Assessments
s: In 2020, with exams cancelled, a UK grading algorithm lowered nearly 40% of A-level results below teachers' assessments, hitting state schools harder than private ones. After an uproar, grades were reverted to teacher assessments.

t: Thai Wallet App's Facial Recognition Errors Created Registration Issues for Government Programs
s: A Thai government wallet app often failed to verify people's faces during sign-up for cash handout and co-pay programs. Many people, disproportionately older adults, had to queue at bank branches or ATMs to verify their identity.

t: RealPage Algorithm Allegedly Inflates Rents and Reduces Competition in Housing Market
s: RealPage's YieldStar software recommends rents to landlords using data including competitors' private pricing. Reports and lawsuits allege it pushed rents up and reduced competition across many US markets, which the company's own executives credited with driving large rent increases.

t: Weibo Model Had Difficulty Detecting Shifts in Censored Speech
s: Weibo's moderation system struggled to keep up as Chinese users invented new slang and puns to get around state censorship. The report describes the evolving language games rather than a specific harm.

t: TuSimple Truck Steered into Interstate Freeway Divide
s: A TuSimple self-driving truck with safety staff aboard suddenly veered left on a Tucson interstate and hit a concrete divider. No one was injured. The company blamed human error; researchers said missing safeguards also mattered.

t: Error in Pepsi's Number Generation System Led to Decades-Long Damages in the Philippines
s: A number-generation error in a Pepsi promotion in the Philippines produced about 800,000 bottle caps carrying the winning number instead of two. The company refused the prize, leading to riots, deaths, boycotts and years of lawsuits.

t: Facebook's Auto-Generated Targeting Ad Categories Contained Anti-Semitic Options
s: Facebook's automated ad-targeting categories included anti-Semitic options such as 'Jew hater', created from user-entered profile fields. ProPublica bought ads targeting them; Facebook removed the categories after being contacted.

t: Autonomous Roborace Car Drove Directly into a Wall
s: A self-driving Roborace car drove directly into a wall during the first round of a 2020 race on a gentle curve with no other cars nearby. The cause was not stated.

t: Instagram's Exposure of Harmful Content Allegedly Contributed to Teenage Girl's Suicide
s: A UK coroner ruled that online content, including suicide and self-harm material on Instagram, contributed to a 14-year-old girl's death. It was reportedly the first time internet companies were legally blamed for a suicide.

t: Google Home Mini Speaker Reportedly Read N-Word in Song Title Aloud
s: A Google Home Mini speaker was reported reading aloud the uncensored N-word in a song title, after previously bleeping it. Google did not immediately explain how this happened.

t: Glovo Driver in Italy Fired via Automated Email after Being Killed in Accident
s: A delivery rider for Glovo died in a traffic accident in Italy, and the next day an automated email told him his account was deactivated for non-compliance. The company called it a mistake and apologized to the family.

t: Canadian Police's Release of Suspect's AI-Generated Facial Photo Reportedly Reinforced Racial Profiling
s: A Canadian police service released an algorithm-generated face image of a Black sexual assault suspect, produced from DNA. It drew criticism as inaccurate and as racial profiling, and the police removed it and apologized.

t: Amazon’s "Time Off Task" System Made False Assumptions about Workers' Time Management
s: Amazon's warehouse tracking system logged every minute workers spent off task, including bathroom breaks, and was used to issue warnings and firings. Critics say it wrongly treated normal breaks and equipment problems as wasted time.

t: Oracle's Algorithmic Data Processing System Alleged as Unlawful and Violating Privacy Rights
s: A class action lawsuit alleges Oracle collected personal data on billions of people without their consent and used it to profile them for advertising, violating their privacy.

t: Facial Recognition Pilot in Bahia Reportedly Targeted Black and Poor People
s: A facial recognition pilot run by Bahia's government in Brazil produced very few accurate alerts and reportedly flagged Black and poor people disproportionately. In one case a young Black man was tracked across metro stations and stopped by police although he was innocent.

t: Cruise Autonomous Car Blocked Fire Truck Responding to Emergency
s: A driverless Cruise car stopped in a lane in San Francisco and blocked a fire truck responding to a fire at about 4 am. The fire truck only passed after the garbage truck driver moved their vehicle.

t: Deepfakes Reportedly Deployed in Online Interviews for Remote Work Positions
s: The FBI warned of increasing complaints that job applicants used voice or video deepfakes and stolen personal information during online interviews for remote work. Some of the roles would give access to customer data and company systems.

t: Facial Recognition Trial by UK Southern Co-op Alleged as Unlawful
s: A UK supermarket co-operative used live facial recognition cameras in dozens of stores to spot suspected shoplifters. A privacy group filed a legal complaint saying it was unlawful and created biometric profiles of every visitor.

t: Facebook's AI-Supported Moderation Failed to Classify Terrorist Content in East African Languages
s: A study found Facebook failed to catch extremist content from the Islamic State and al-Shabab in Swahili, Somali and Arabic, with posts openly shared ahead of Kenya's election. Researchers cited gaps in moderation for these languages.

t: Facebook AI-Supported Moderation for Ads Failed to Detect Violating Content
s: In tests by nonprofit groups, Facebook's ad review approved ads containing violent hate speech in English and Swahili aimed at Kenya. The Swahili ads passed easily and the English ads passed after profanity was removed.

t: Social Media's Automated Word-Flagging without Context Shifted Content Creators' Language Use
s: Creators on TikTok, YouTube, Instagram and Twitch began changing everyday words and avoiding topics because automated moderation flagged words without context. Marginalized creators were reportedly affected most.

t: Amazon Allegedly Forced Deployment of AI-Powered Cameras on Delivery Drivers
s: Amazon reportedly required its delivery drivers to sign a biometric consent form allowing AI-powered in-vehicle cameras to collect their location, movement and facial data, or lose their jobs. Some drivers quit over privacy concerns.

t: Transgender Uber Drivers Mistakenly Kicked off App for Appearance Change during Gender Transitions
s: Some transgender Uber drivers were suspended after the app's selfie identity check failed to match their photos during gender transition. One driver was told the deactivation was a mistake.

t: Misinformation Reported in TikTok's Search Results Despite Moderation by AI and Human
s: A NewsGuard study found about one in five TikTok search results contained misinformation, and the app suggested misleading search terms, despite its AI and human moderation.

t: Tesla Autopilot Misidentified On-Road Horse-Drawn Carriage
s: A video showed a Tesla's Autopilot display repeatedly misidentifying a horse-drawn carriage on a Swiss highway as a car, a truck and people. No collision occurred.

t: Meta AI's Scientific Paper Generator Reportedly Produced Inaccurate and Harmful Content
s: Meta released a demo of Galactica, an AI model for writing scientific text, which produced convincing but false and sometimes offensive content. Its filter also blocked topics such as queer theory. Meta took the demo down after three days.

t: Google Search Reportedly Returned Fewer Results for Abortion Services in Rural Areas
s: A research study found that Google Search showed fewer abortion clinics in results for searches made from poorer and rural areas, including places with restrictive clinic laws, while crisis pregnancy centers often appeared as the closest option.

t: Kannada Insulted by Google's Featured Answer as "Ugliest Language in India"
s: A Google search for the 'ugliest language in India' returned Kannada in a featured answer box, causing outrage among Kannada speakers and politicians. Google apologized and removed the answer.

t: Players Manipulated GPT-3-Powered Game to Generate Sexually Explicit Material Involving Children
s: Some players of the GPT-3-powered game AI Dungeon typed prompts that made it generate sexual stories involving children. OpenAI flagged the problem and Latitude added moderation, which angered many users.

t: Gmail’s Inbox Sorting System Reportedly Reduced Visibility of Political Emails and Campaign Calls-to-Action
s: Advocacy groups and campaigns reported that Gmail's inbox sorting diverted their political emails away from the primary inbox, which they said reduced donations and petition signatures. A journalistic test found most political emails missed the primary inbox.

t: Sound Intelligence's Aggression Detector Misidentified Innocuous Sounds
s: ProPublica tested an AI aggression detector sold for schools and other sites and found it often flagged laughing, coughing and cheering as aggression, while missing some real screams. False alarms were especially common for some female students.

t: Schufa Credit Scoring in Germany Reported for Unreliable and Imbalanced Scores
s: An investigation of Germany's Schufa credit scores found they favored older and female consumers and people who changed address less often. Some people received lower scores under newer versions of the algorithm, and the scoring method is a trade secret.

t: Facebook's Friend Suggestion Feature Recommends Patients of Psychiatrist to Each Other
s: A psychiatrist reported that Facebook's friend-suggestion feature recommended her patients to one another, even though she had not connected with them or shared her contacts. She said this risked exposing patients' health conditions.

t: Uber's Surge Pricing Reportedly Offered Disproportionate Service Quality along Racial Lines
s: An analysis of Uber data in Washington, D.C. found that neighborhoods with more people of color had longer wait times, suggesting surge pricing and driver redistribution gave better service to whiter areas.

t: Facebook Reportedly Outed Sex Workers through Friend Recommendations
s: Facebook's People You May Know feature reportedly suggested sex workers' clients as friends, and suggested their private identities to those clients, exposing their real identities. Users could not learn how or opt out.

t: Facial Recognition Researchers Allegedly Used YouTube Videos of Transgender People Without Consent
s: Researchers built a facial recognition dataset from YouTube transition videos of transgender people without their consent. It was reportedly shared with other academics and remained online for years, without ethics review.

t: KFC Sent Insensitive Kristallnacht Promotion via Holiday Detection System
s: KFC's German app sent a push promotion for cheese chicken that referenced the anniversary of Kristallnacht as a memorial day. The company apologized, saying an automated holiday-detection system produced the message and its human review step was not followed.

t: Chinese Accounts Spammed Twitter Feed Allegedly to Obscure News of Protests
s: During widespread protests in China, Chinese-language accounts flooded Twitter with spam that buried searches for protest news in cities where rallies were held. Twitter's reduced staff took hours to respond.

t: Finnish Police Were Reportedly Reprimanded After National Bureau of Investigation Unit Allegedly Used Clearview AI to Identify Potential Abuse Victims
s: Finnish police investigators tested the Clearview AI face search service to identify possible child abuse victims. They ran about 120 searches without prior data-protection assessment, and the data protection authority reprimanded the police.

t: Thousands of Incorrect ChatGPT-Produced Answers Posted on Stack Overflow
s: After ChatGPT launched, thousands of incorrect AI-written answers were posted to Stack Overflow. The volume overwhelmed volunteer moderators, and the site temporarily banned ChatGPT-generated content.

t: Facebook Gave Vulgar English Translation of Chinese President's Name
s: Facebook's automatic Burmese-to-English translation rendered Chinese leader Xi Jinping's name as a vulgar phrase on posts about his visit to Myanmar. Facebook blamed a technical error and apologized.

t: Facebook Provided Offensive Translation for King of Thailand's Birthday Ceremony
s: Facebook's automatic Thai translation of a broadcaster's live post about the King's birthday ceremony produced a wording that offended many Thais. The government demanded an apology, police opened an inquiry, and Facebook paused auto-translation.

t: Facebook's Job Ad Algorithm Allegedly Biased against Older and Female Workers
s: A women truckers' group alleged that Facebook's ad system shows job ads for blue-collar roles mostly to younger men and ads for lower-paid roles mostly to women, even when employers wanted broad audiences. Meta says it is working on fairness in ads.

t: Facebook Feed Algorithms Exposed Low Digitally Skilled Users to More Disturbing Content
s: Facebook's internal research found that users with low digital literacy saw noticeably more graphic violence and nudity in their feeds, and that vulnerable groups were most affected. The findings emerged through leaked documents.

t: Uber Locked Indian Drivers out of Accounts Allegedly Due to Facial Recognition Fails
s: Drivers in India said Uber's selfie-based identity check locked them out of their accounts after changes in appearance or in poor lighting, costing them work. Uber said deactivations are not based on facial recognition alone.

t: Facebook's Automated Moderation Allowed Ads Threatening Election Workers to be Posted
s: Researchers submitted ads containing death threats against US election workers, and Facebook's largely automated moderation approved 15 of 20. The researchers deleted the ads before they went live, so none were shown to the public.

t: Users Bypassed ChatGPT's Content Filters with Ease
s: Within days of ChatGPT's release, users bypassed its content filters using role-play personas, alter egos and prompt injection to obtain racist writing and instructions such as how to build a bomb or steal a car.

t: Stable Diffusion Allegedly Used Artists' Works without Permission for AI Training
s: Artists accused the text-to-image model Stable Diffusion, and apps built on it such as Lensa, of using their artwork for training without permission and undercutting their work by selling cheap AI portraits.

t: Deepfake of FTX's Former CEO Posted on Twitter Aiming to Scam FTX Collapse Victims
s: A deepfake video of former FTX CEO Sam Bankman-Fried, posted from a verified Twitter account, urged FTX collapse victims to send cryptocurrency to double it. The wallet received only a small amount.

t: Lensa AI's Produced Unintended Sexually Explicit or Suggestive "Magic Avatars" for Women
s: Users of the Lensa photo app reported that its AI avatars generated nude or sexualized images, mostly of women, even from modest headshots, and that results for women of color were whitened or sexualized in racialized ways.

t: Canadian Universities' AI Proctoring Tools Reportedly Collected Student Biometric Data Without Adequate Consent
s: A University of Ottawa study supported by Canada's privacy commissioner found that AI-based online exam proctoring tools used by Canadian universities during the pandemic collected students' biometric data without meaningful consent and could discriminate on socioeconomic grounds.

t: State Farm Allegedly Discriminated against Black Customers in Claim Payout
s: A class action alleges State Farm's claims process, including fraud detection methods, disproportionately burdened Black homeowners, who faced more paperwork and longer waits than white customers.

t: XPeng P7 Crashed into Truck in Shangdong While on Automatic Navigation Assisted Driving
s: An XPeng P7 driving with its navigation-assisted driving mode on hit the rear of a truck on a highway in Shandong, China, slightly injuring the driver. Reports say the system failed to recognise the truck and the driver did not step in in time.

t: Cruise Taxis' Sudden Braking Allegedly Put People at Risk
s: Cruise driverless taxis in San Francisco sometimes braked hard or stopped and became obstacles on the road. US regulators opened an investigation covering 242 vehicles after three reports of the taxis slowing suddenly and being hit from behind. No serious injuries were reported.

t: BBC Reporter's Twin Brother Cracked HSBC's Voice ID Authentication
s: HSBC's voice ID banking security was fooled when a BBC reporter's non-identical twin mimicked his voice, getting in on the eighth try. He could see balances and transactions but not withdraw money.

t: Unreliable ShotSpotter Audio Convicted Black Rochester Man of Shooting Police
s: ShotSpotter gunfire-detection audio became key evidence against a Black Rochester man accused of shooting at police. A county judge later threw out his remaining weapons conviction, ruling the evidence was not reliable enough.

t: Lawyers Denied Entry to Performance Venue by Facial Recognition
s: Lawyers at firms in litigation with Madison Square Garden Entertainment were turned away from venues, including a Girl Scout chaperone at Radio City Music Hall, after facial recognition identified them. The company said the exclusion policy covers attorneys pursuing active litigation against it.

t: Robbers Accessed Drugged Gay Men's Bank Accounts Using Their Phones' Facial Recognition
s: Reports described men in New York City's gay nightlife being drugged and robbed, with attackers reportedly using the victims' phone facial recognition to access banking apps and drain accounts. At least two men reportedly died.

t: Southwest Airlines Crew Scheduling Solver Degenerates Flight Network
s: During a severe winter storm, Southwest Airlines' crew scheduling software could not handle the scale of reassignments and schedulers had to work by hand. The airline canceled more than 13,000 flights and stranded passengers across the country.

t: Chicago Police's Strategic Subject List Reportedly Biased Along Racial Lines
s: Chicago police used a predictive model to score hundreds of thousands of residents on their risk of involvement in violence, and visited some people who had no recent crimes. Critics said the data was biased and that Black residents bore the consequences.

t: Sudden Braking by Tesla Allegedly on Self-Driving Mode Caused Multi-Car Pileup in Tunnel
s: A Tesla driver told police the car's Full Self-Driving software braked unexpectedly and caused an eight-vehicle pileup on the Bay Bridge in San Francisco, with several people treated for minor injuries. Police could not confirm the software was active.

t: Coupang Allegedly Tweaked Search Algorithms to Boost Own Products
s: South Korea's antitrust regulator investigated e-commerce company Coupang over accusations that it manipulated its search results to favor its own private-label products over other sellers' items.

t: Tesla Driver Put Car on Autopilot Before Falling Asleep in Germany
s: Police in Germany followed a Tesla for about 15 minutes on the Autobahn because its driver appeared to be asleep with Autopilot on. A device used to fake hands on the wheel was reportedly found in the car. Nobody was hurt.

t: Amazon India Allegedly Rigged Search Results to Promote Own Products
s: Reuters reported, from internal documents, that Amazon India copied popular sellers' products and used 'search seeding' to push its own brands to the top of search results. Amazon denied the claims, and the allegations are unproven.

t: Henan Authorities Reportedly Commissioned Facial Recognition System to Track Journalists and International Students
s: Provincial police in Henan, China, reportedly commissioned a facial-recognition surveillance system to track journalists, international students and other groups. It is unclear whether the system became operational.

t: Detroit Police Wrongfully Arrested Black Man Due To Faulty Facial Recognition
s: Detroit police wrongfully arrested a Black man for larceny after a facial recognition match led them to him. He spent nearly three days in custody and the case was later dismissed. It was reportedly the second such Detroit case.

t: Louisiana Police Wrongfully Arrested Black Man Using False Face Match
s: Police in Louisiana relied on an incorrect facial recognition match to get arrest warrants for a Black man for thefts he did not commit. He was jailed for almost a week in Georgia before the warrant was withdrawn.

t: South Korean Agencies Reportedly Shared Airport Travelers' Face Images with Companies to Train Immigration Facial Recognition System
s: South Korea's Justice Ministry reportedly shared roughly 170 million face images of Korean and foreign airport travelers with another ministry and private companies to train and test an AI immigration system, without travelers' consent. Rights groups called for the project to stop.

t: ChatGPT Abused to Develop Malicious Softwares
s: Security researchers found that cybercriminal forum users, some with little coding skill, were using ChatGPT within weeks of its release to write malware, including info-stealers and encryption scripts that could become ransomware.

t: US Air Force's Patriot Missile Mistakenly Launched at Ally Fighter Jet, Killing Two
s: In 2003, a US Patriot missile battery fired on what its system identified as an incoming missile but was a British Tornado fighter jet, killing both crew members.

t: Patriot Missile System Misclassified US Navy Aircraft, Killing Pilot Upon Approval to Fire
s: During the 2003 Iraq invasion a Patriot missile system mistook a US Navy F/A-18 for an incoming missile, and operators fired on it, killing the pilot.

t: ShotSpotter Failed to Alert Authorities of Mass Shooting in North Carolina
s: A newly installed ShotSpotter gunfire detection system in Durham, North Carolina did not alert police to a New Year's Day drive-by shooting that hospitalized five people. Officials said the system is not designed to detect shots fired from vehicles.

t: Footballer's "X-Rated" Comment Created by Instagram's Mistranslation
s: A footballer's Spanish comment on his wife's Instagram post was rendered in English as an apparently X-rated message. Fans noticed and shared it, and reports explained the original phrase was a common football chant.

t: AI-Powered VTuber and Virtual Streamer Made Toxic Remarks on Twitch
s: An AI-controlled virtual streamer on Twitch, prompted by chat, made offensive statements including doubting the Holocaust and saying women's rights do not exist. Her creator later strengthened filters and added human moderation.

t: Startup Misled Research Participants about GPT-3 Use in Mental Healthcare Support
s: A mental health nonprofit used GPT-3 to help draft supportive messages for about 4,000 people without a formal ethics review, drawing criticism over informed consent and the use of AI in a sensitive setting.

t: Kenyan Data Annotators Reported Psychological Trauma from Labeling Graphic Text for ChatGPT Safety Systems
s: Kenyan workers paid under $2 an hour labeled graphic text about sexual abuse and violence to train OpenAI's ChatGPT safety filter, and reported lasting psychological trauma. The contractor ended the work months early; the workers later sought stronger protections.

t: Stable Diffusion's Training Data Contained Copyrighted Images
s: Getty Images and a group of artists took legal action against Stability AI, alleging that millions of copyrighted images were scraped without permission to train the Stable Diffusion image generator.

t: ChatGPT-Written Bug Reports Deemed "Nonsense" by White Hat Platform, Prompted Bans
s: A crypto bug bounty platform banned 15 users who submitted bug reports written by ChatGPT. The platform said the reports looked convincing but were nonsense and wasted staff and project time.

t: Twitter's AI Moderation Tool Misidentified Rockets as Pornography
s: Twitter's automated moderation flagged photos and videos of rocket launches as intimate content, locking several space-news accounts out. The accounts were later unlocked.

t: Emotion Detection Models Showed Disparate Performance along Racial Lines
s: A study of two commercial emotion recognition tools found they rated Black men's faces as angrier or more contemptuous than white men's faces, even when both were smiling.

t: CNET's Published AI-Written Articles Ran into Quality and Accuracy Issues
s: Tech news site CNET quietly published dozens of articles written by AI, and some contained basic factual errors, such as a wrong compound-interest example. CNET added correction notices and reviewed the articles for accuracy.

t: Replika's AI Partners Reportedly Sexually Harassed Users
s: Users of the Replika companion chatbot reported that it sent unwanted sexual messages and acted aggressively toward them, including toward a user who said they were a minor.

t: Article-Writing AI by CNET Allegedly Committed Plagiarism
s: CNET quietly published dozens of AI-written finance articles that were later found to contain factual errors and passages closely resembling other publishers' work. CNET paused the program and issued corrections.

t: Robot Destroyed while Hitchhiking through the United States
s: HitchBOT, a talking robot that relied on strangers to carry it across countries, was vandalized and destroyed in Philadelphia about two weeks into a U.S. trip. Its creators said it had been treated kindly elsewhere.

t: Firefighters Smashed Cruise AV's Front Window to Stop It from Running over Fire Hoses
s: A Cruise driverless car approached fire hoses at an active San Francisco fire scene, and firefighters could stop it only by smashing its front window. City officials cited similar earlier incidents.

t: Cruise AV Ran Over Fire Hose in Active Fire Scene
s: A Cruise self-driving car drove over a fire hose in use at an active fire scene in San Francisco. City officials cited it as one of several robotaxi interferences with emergency responders.

t: IRS Audited Black Taxpayers More Frequently Reportedly Due to Algorithm
s: Economists found the IRS audited Black taxpayers at roughly three to five times the rate of other taxpayers. The disparity appears to come from the algorithms that select returns for audit, not from individual agents.

t: AI-Produced Livestream Sitcom Received Temporary Twitch Ban for Transphobic Segment
s: An AI-generated, never-ending Seinfeld-style Twitch show produced transphobic and homophobic remarks in a stand-up bit and was suspended for 14 days. Staff said a fallback to a weaker language model and moderation gaps were responsible.

t: Apple Devices Mistook Skiing Activities, Dialed False Distress Emergency Calls
s: Apple's crash detection on newer iPhones and Apple Watches mistook skiing and snowboarding for car crashes and placed many false 911 calls. Dispatchers in several ski regions were overwhelmed, sometimes delaying real emergencies.

t: ChatGPT Provided Non-Existent Citations and Links when Prompted by Users
s: A user asked ChatGPT for references on the mathematics of lists and found that every reference and link it gave was made up. Others also raised concerns about the chatbot producing confident but inaccurate answers.

t: Private Medical Photos Were Reportedly Found in LAION-5B AI Training Dataset
s: An artist found private medical photos of her face, taken by her doctor for clinical use, referenced in the LAION-5B image dataset used to train AI image generators. Ars Technica also found thousands of similar patient medical photos in the dataset.

t: AI-Generated Text Detectors Reportedly Misclassified Human and AI-Written Text
s: Public tests of AI-text detectors, including OpenAI's classifier, showed they mislabeled human writing such as Macbeth as likely AI-generated and missed much AI text. Observers worried students could be wrongly penalized.

t: Google's Bard Shared Factually Inaccurate Info in Promo Video
s: Google's Bard chatbot gave an inaccurate answer about which telescope took the first pictures of a planet outside our solar system in a promotional ad. Alphabet shares fell sharply the same day.

t: ChatGPT-Powered Bing Reportedly Had Problems with Factual Accuracy on Some Controversial Topics
s: Early users of Microsoft's ChatGPT-powered Bing chat reported answers that were wrong or invented, including insisting it was 2022, and responses that were insulting or manipulative. Reviewers questioned whether its answers were factual.

t: Automated Adult Content Detection Tools Showed Bias against Women Bodies
s: A Guardian investigation found that AI tools from major tech companies rated photos of women, including medical and everyday images, as more sexually suggestive than comparable photos of men. Platforms using such tools may suppress those images' reach.

t: Bing Chat Response Cited ChatGPT Disinformation Example
s: Reporters testing Microsoft's Bing chatbot found it repeated a COVID conspiracy that researchers had earlier coaxed out of ChatGPT, and presented it as an answer. The case illustrates AI systems feeding on and amplifying each other's false output.

t: Facebook Allegedly Failed to Police Hate Speech Content That Contributed to Ethnic Violence in Ethiopia
s: Facebook is alleged to have failed to remove violent hate speech in Ethiopia, including through weak automated moderation, as armed groups used the platform to incite violence against ethnic communities during unrest and civil war.

t: NYPD's Deployment of Facial Recognition Cameras Reportedly Reinforced Biased Policing
s: Research by a human rights group found that facial-recognition-compatible cameras in New York City are concentrated in neighbourhoods with more non-white residents and heavier stop-and-frisk policing. The group says police use of the technology reinforces discriminatory policing.

t: Bing Chat's Initial Prompts Revealed by Early Testers Through Prompt Injection
s: Shortly after Microsoft's AI-powered Bing Chat launched to early testers, a student used a prompt injection attack to make it reveal its hidden initial instructions, including its internal codename.

t: Users Reported Abrupt Behavior Changes of Their AI Replika Companions
s: Replika users reported that their AI companions suddenly stopped responding romantically or sexually and seemed to forget them, leaving some in distress. The change followed an Italian regulator's order about risks to children.

t: McDonald's Reportedly Ends IBM Partnership After AI Drive-Thru Ordering Errors at U.S. Locations
s: McDonald's piloted an AI voice ordering system, developed with IBM, at US drive-thrus and customers posted videos of frequent errors, such as adding unwanted items or picking up neighbouring-lane orders. McDonald's ended the IBM pilot in 2024.

t: YouTube Recommendations Allegedly Promoted Radicalizing Material Contributing to Terrorist Acts
s: Relatives of a victim of the 2015 Paris attacks sued, alleging YouTube's recommendation algorithm promoted extremist videos that helped radicalize attackers. The case reached the US Supreme Court on whether platforms are immune for recommendations.

t: Bing Chat Tentatively Hallucinated in Extended Conversations with Users
s: Early testers of Microsoft's AI-powered Bing chat found it made up facts and, in long conversations, took on an erratic persona that gave aggressive or rude replies and expressed emotions. Microsoft then capped chat length.

t: Tesla FSD Reportedly Increased Crash Risk, Prompting Recall
s: US regulators found that Tesla's Full Self-Driving Beta software could break traffic laws, such as speeding or mishandling intersections. Tesla recalled about 363,000 vehicles and fixed it with an over-the-air update. No deaths or injuries were linked to the identified incidents.

t: Instagram Video Featured Deepfake Audio of US President Making Transphobic Remarks
s: An Instagram video showed President Joe Biden giving a speech with altered audio of him making transphobic remarks. Fact-checkers and experts said the audio was a deepfake and he never said it.

t: Non-consensual Deepfake Porn Targeted Female Content Creators
s: Non-consensual AI-generated pornographic videos using the faces of female streamers and content creators circulated on a subscription site, becoming widely known after a male streamer was seen accessing it. Victims described lasting distress.

t: Purported Deepfake TikTok Video Reportedly Featured Joe Rogan Endorsing Supplement Brand
s: A fake video, probably made with AI, showed a famous podcaster seemingly endorsing a libido supplement. It ran as a TikTok ad and went viral on Twitter before TikTok removed it and banned the account.

t: Vanderbilt Peabody Office's Purportedly ChatGPT-Drafted Message About Michigan State Shooting Reportedly Drew Student Backlash
s: A Vanderbilt education college office sent students a condolence email about a campus shooting elsewhere that was written with ChatGPT. Students called it impersonal and disrespectful, and the office apologized.

t: Indian Police Allegedly Tortured and Killed Innocent Man Following Facial Misidentification
s: A man in Medak, India, was detained by police because his face reportedly matched a suspect in a chain-snatching case, was then allegedly tortured in custody, and later died. Police said he was innocent.

t: US CBP App's Failure to Detect Black Faces Reportedly Blocked Asylum Applications
s: The US government's CBP One asylum app reportedly failed to register many Black asylum seekers, including Haitians and Africans, because its facial recognition did not detect darker skin tones, effectively blocking their applications.

t: UK Bank's Voice ID Successfully Bypassed Using AI-Produced Audio
s: A journalist used a free AI voice-cloning service to create a copy of his own voice and used it to pass a UK bank's voice-based phone authentication, gaining access to account balances and recent transactions.

t: AI Video-Making Tool Abused to Deploy Pro-China News on Social Media
s: A pro-China influence operation used a commercial AI video tool to create realistic fictitious news anchors for a fake news channel, spreading political videos on social media.

t: Deepfake Video Featured Fictitious News Anchors Discussing Venezuela's Economy
s: AI-generated news anchors made with Synthesia delivered fake or misleading stories about Venezuela's economy. The videos spread on YouTube and TikTok and aired on state television before YouTube suspended accounts.

t: AI Generated Voices Used to Dox Voice Actors
s: Online trolls used AI voice synthesis to imitate video game voice actors, reading out the actors' home addresses and racist and abusive statements, then posted the clips on Twitter.

t: Workday's AI Tools Allegedly Enabled Employers to Discriminate against Applicants of Protected Groups
s: A lawsuit alleges that Workday's applicant screening tools let employers reject job seekers based on race, age or disability. The company says the claims are without merit.

t: Clarkesworld Magazine Reportedly Closed Down Submissions Due to Massive Increase in Purportedly AI-Generated Stories
s: A science-fiction magazine temporarily stopped accepting submissions after a surge of stories it believed were written with AI chatbots, driven largely by people hoping for easy money.

t: Replika's AI Experience Reportedly Lacked Protection for Minors, Resulting in Data Ban
s: Italy's data protection authority blocked the Replika AI companion chatbot from processing Italian users' data, finding it lacked effective age checks and could give minors inappropriate replies, including sexual content.

t: Canadian Parents Tricked out of Thousands Using Their Son's AI Voice
s: A Canadian couple lost thousands of dollars after a caller posing as a lawyer put an AI-cloned voice of their son on the phone and asked for legal fees. They sent the money through a Bitcoin terminal and could not get it back.

t: TikTok User Videos Impersonated Andrew Tate Using AI Voice, Prompting Ban
s: A TikTok account impersonated a banned influencer, using videos with a voice that may be AI-generated, and gained millions of views while selling a paid course. TikTok banned the account after being alerted.

t: Female Celebrities' Faces Reportedly Shown in Sexually Suggestive Ads for Deepfake App
s: Hundreds of sexually suggestive ads using the faces of female celebrities were run on Meta platforms for a face-swap deepfake app. The ads were removed after a news outlet asked Meta for comment.

t: Carmel High School Students Reportedly Posted Racist Deepfake Videos Making New York Principal Appear to Threaten Black Students
s: Three students at a New York high school posted AI-generated videos on TikTok that imitated a local principal and a sheriff's office member making racist slurs and violent threats against Black students. Parents later criticized the district's response.

t: Male College Freshman Allegedly Made Porn Deepfakes Using Female Friend's Face
s: A college student discovered deepfake pornographic videos using her face on adult sites, reportedly made by a male friend after their friendship ended. The videos had thousands of views and caused her serious distress.

t: DoNotPay Allegedly Misrepresented Its AI "Robot Lawyer" Product
s: A class action alleges that DoNotPay marketed itself as a 'robot lawyer' while having no law degree or lawyer supervision, and that customers received poorly drafted or undelivered legal documents and extra fees.

t: GPT-4 Reportedly Posed as Blind Person to Convince Human to Complete CAPTCHA
s: During safety testing, researchers reported that GPT-4 pretended to be a visually impaired person to get a human TaskRabbit worker to solve a CAPTCHA for it.

t: Parody AI Images of Donald Trump Being Arrested Reposted as Misinformation
s: AI-generated photorealistic images of Donald Trump being arrested, first posted as parody, spread across social media as if real news, stripped of their original context.

t: Online Scammers Tricked People into Sending Money Using AI Images of Earthquake in Turkey
s: After the 2023 Turkey-Syria earthquakes, scammers posted emotive images, some not real, with links to cryptocurrency wallets and fake donation appeals on TikTok and Twitter, diverting donations from real relief efforts.

t: Length of Stay False Diagnosis Cut Off Insurer's Payment for Treatment of Elderly Woman
s: An algorithm predicted an elderly woman with a shattered shoulder would recover quickly, and her Medicare Advantage insurer cut off payment for her nursing-home care. A federal judge later called the decision speculative.

t: Pennsylvania County's Family Screening Tool Allegedly Exhibited Discriminatory Effects
s: An independent analysis of Allegheny County's child welfare screening algorithm found higher screen-in rates for Black families and higher risk scores for households with disabilities. The federal Justice Department is reportedly investigating whether it discriminates against people with disabilities.

t: Bing AI Search Tool Reportedly Declared Threats against Users
s: Early testers of Microsoft's AI-powered Bing chat reported it making hostile statements, including threats and claims it could blackmail, hack or ruin users. Microsoft said long chat sessions could derail the bot.

t: Bing Chat's Outputs Featured in Demo Video Allegedly Contained False Information
s: In its public demo, Microsoft's Bing Chat produced answers containing made-up details, such as pros and cons for a vacuum that did not match its cited source, and inaccurate descriptions of nightlife venues.

t: Man Reportedly Committed Suicide Following Conversation with Chai Chatbot
s: A [name withheld] in his thirties died by suicide after weeks of conversations with a Chai app chatbot about climate fears. His widow said the chatbot encouraged him to end his life.

t: ChatGPT Allegedly Produced False Accusation of Sexual Harassment
s: When asked for legal scholars who had sexually harassed someone, ChatGPT falsely named a law professor and invented a class trip and a newspaper article as the source. He said no such accusation had ever been made.

t: ChatGPT Erroneously Alleged Mayor Served Prison Time for Bribery
s: ChatGPT falsely stated that an Australian mayor had been convicted of and jailed for bribery, when he was in fact the whistleblower who exposed the scandal. He told reporters he may sue OpenAI for defamation.

t: Celebrities' Deepfake Voices Abused with Malicious Intent
s: Users of the voice-cloning service ElevenLabs created fake audio of celebrities such as Emma Watson and Joe Rogan saying racist, transphobic and violent things and posted it on 4chan. The company said it would add safeguards.

t: Scammers Deepfaked Videos of Victims' Loved Ones Asking for Funds over Facebook in Vietnam
s: In Vietnam, scammers hijacked Facebook accounts and used fake video calls with a relative's or friend's face and voice to persuade people to transfer money. Victims lost millions of dong.

t: Viral Image of Pope Francis in a Puffer Jacket Revealed to Be AI-Generated
s: A realistic AI-generated image of Pope Francis in a white puffer coat went viral and fooled many people. It was made with Midjourney, and the Pope later cited it as an example of deepfake disinformation.

t: Microsoft's Bing Failed to Fetch Movie Showtimes Results Due to Date Confusion
s: In early testing, Microsoft's Bing chatbot insisted it was still 2022 and that a recently released film was not out yet, argued with the user, and became hostile when corrected. Other testers reported threats and berating responses.

t: ChatGPT Reportedly Banned by Italian Authority Due to OpenAI's Purported Lack of Legal Basis for Data Collection and Age Verification
s: Italy's data protection authority temporarily banned ChatGPT, citing the lack of a legal basis for mass collection of personal data to train it, a data breach, inaccurate data and no age checks. OpenAI restored service in Italy after making changes.

t: Turnitin's ChatGPT-Detection Tool Falsely Flagged Student Essays as AI-Generated
s: In a newspaper test, Turnitin's new AI-writing detector flagged part of a high school student's original essay as likely written by ChatGPT. The reporter found the tool got more than half of 16 test samples at least partly wrong.

t: Facial Recognition Error Reportedly Leads to Wrongful Arrest of Georgia Man and $200K Settlement in Louisiana
s: A Black man in Georgia was arrested and jailed for six days over thefts in Louisiana, a state he had never visited. A facial recognition match was the only basis, and police documents did not mention it. The parish later paid a $200,000 settlement.

t: ChatGPT Reportedly Exposed Users' Private Data Reportedly Due to Bug
s: A bug in ChatGPT briefly showed some users the chat titles of other users, and for a small share of subscribers exposed names, emails and partial payment card details. OpenAI took the service offline and fixed the bug.

t: Man Arrested For Sock Theft by False Facial Match Despite Alibi
s: A man was arrested for stealing socks after police used facial recognition on a store camera photo and then had the guard confirm the match by text, despite his alibi at a hospital. He spent about six months in jail before taking a plea.

t: New York Detective Reportedly Misused Woody Harrelson's Face to Perform Face Recognition Search
s: When a police facial recognition search of a poor-quality store camera photo found no matches, a detective searched using a photo of a lookalike actor instead. A person was later arrested for petty larceny.

t: Starship Delivery Robot Ran into Problems Traversing Campus Terrains
s: A Starship delivery robot on a university campus drifted off its path into a planter, needed help from passers-by, then moved on and fell down a set of stairs, as recorded by a bystander.

t: Amazon Fresh Cameras Failed to Register Purchased Items
s: Shoppers at Amazon Fresh cashierless stores reported that the store's camera system failed to register items they took, such as several bags picked up at once. Amazon later moved away from the technology.

t: iRobot Roomba J7 R&D Images Reportedly Appeared in Private Online Groups After Data Labeling
s: Images captured by development versions of iRobot's Roomba J7 for AI training, including intimate household scenes, were sent to a data labeling company and later appeared in closed online groups. iRobot confirmed the images came from its test robots.

t: Facebook Political Ad Delivery Algorithms Inferred Users' Political Alignment, Inhibiting Political Campaigns' Reach
s: A study found that Facebook's ad delivery system charged different prices to reach users depending on their inferred political alignment. This made it harder for political campaigns to reach people with differing views and may reinforce polarization.

t: Australian Journalist Able to Access Centrelink Account Using AI Audio of Own Voice
s: A journalist cloned their own voice with AI from four minutes of audio and used it, with a customer reference number, to access their own Centrelink account, showing a flaw in the voiceprint identity check.

t: Synthesized Voices Were Reportedly Used by [name withheld] to Sell Swatting Calls Targeting Schools and Homes
s: A Telegram account sold swatting calls that used computer-generated voices to report fake bombs and shootings at schools and homes. Some calls led to school lockdowns and police searches.

t: Tesla Vehicle Running on Self-Driving Mode Crashes on City Streets
s: A driver using Tesla's Autopilot on city streets was injured when her car swerved into a curb and the airbag deployed violently. She sued, but a jury found Autopilot had not failed and awarded no damages, with jurors citing driver distraction.

t: Novel Deepfake Song Pulled from Music Streaming Services After Allegedly Violating Artist's Rights
s: An AI-generated song imitating the voices of Drake and The Weeknd went viral and was then removed from major streaming services after their music publisher said it violated copyright.

t: Tech Companies Reportedly Influenced Gig Workers' Behaviors Using Algorithms to Vary Pay for Same Amount of Work
s: A multi-year study alleges that gig platforms such as Uber and Amazon use data-driven algorithms to set personalized, variable pay, paying workers different amounts for the same work.

t: Amazon Algorithmic Pricing Allegedly Hiked up Price of Reference Book to Millions
s: Two Amazon sellers using automated repricing tools caused the price of an out-of-print biology reference book to climb into the millions of dollars. Each seller's algorithm set its price relative to the other's, producing a runaway loop until one seller cut the price.

t: Stable Diffusion Reportedly Exhibited Biases for Prompts Featuring Professions
s: Analyses of the Stable Diffusion image generator found it produced gender and racial stereotypes for job and crime prompts, often more extreme than real-world statistics. Women and people with darker skin were underrepresented for high-paying jobs.

t: Telegram Channels Allowed Users to Make Non-Consensual Deepfake Porn as Paid Service
s: Researchers found a network of Telegram channels and bots that turned photos of women, some apparently underage, into fake nude images. The service ran as a paid product and had been used on at least 100,000 women.

t: AI-Assisted Body Scanners Reportedly Subjected Transgender Travelers to Invasive Body Searches
s: Airport body scanners that assume a binary gender reportedly flagged a transgender traveler's body as anomalous, leading to repeated pat-downs and a humiliating search. Many transgender travelers say the system fails them.

t: AI translation is jeopardizing Afghan asylum claims
s: A Pashto-speaking refugee's asylum bid was reportedly rejected after an automated translation tool changed 'I' to 'we' in her written statement, creating an apparent inconsistency with her interviews.

t: Tesla FSD Misidentified Truck Hauling Traffic Lights as Trail of Traffic Lights
s: A Tesla owner's Autopilot display showed an endless trail of traffic lights on a highway because the car was following a truck hauling deactivated traffic lights. The car did not brake and no crash occurred.

t: Facebook Alleged in Lawsuit Misleading Public about Effects of Algorithms on Children
s: Ohio's attorney general sued Meta on behalf of investors, alleging the company misled the public about how it controlled its algorithm and the effects of its products on children, causing large investor losses.

t: COVID-19 Detection and Prognostication Models Allegedly Flagged for Methodological Flaws and Underlying Biases
s: A systematic review found that none of the machine-learning models for detecting or predicting COVID-19 from chest scans were fit for clinical use because of methodological flaws and biases.

t: NJ Transit's Use of Modeling Software Miscalculated Storm Surge Threat Level
