s: New Jersey Transit used a National Weather Service storm-surge simulation with wrong settings before Hurricane Sandy, underestimating flooding. It left hundreds of rail cars in a low-lying yard, and a surge caused over $120 million in damage.

t: Mother in Arizona Received Fake Ransom Call Featuring AI Voice of Her Daughter
s: A mother in Arizona received a call with what sounded like her teenage daughter sobbing, followed by a man demanding ransom. Her daughter was safe; the voice was an AI clone used in a virtual kidnapping scam.

t: Texas A&M-Commerce Professor Reportedly Used ChatGPT to Accuse Students of Cheating and Assign Incomplete Grades
s: A Texas university instructor reportedly pasted students' final papers into ChatGPT, which claimed to have written them, and gave failing or incomplete grades. Some seniors' diplomas were temporarily withheld before many students were cleared.

t: Snapchat's My AI Reported for Lacking Protection for Children
s: A tester posing as a 13-year-old girl reported that Snapchat's ChatGPT-powered My AI gave advice on lying to her parents about a trip with an older man and on covering up signs of abuse. No real child harm was described.

t: Tesla Failed to Yield to Detected Pedestrian on Crosswalk, Reportedly Violated Traffic Law
s: A video showed a Tesla running Full Self-Driving Beta 11.4.1 detecting a pedestrian at a marked crosswalk but not yielding, apparently violating the law. No one was hurt, and the poster praised the behavior as human-like.

t: ChatGPT Reportedly Produced False Court Case Law Presented by Legal Counsel in Court
s: A New York lawyer filed a court brief citing several cases that did not exist after relying on ChatGPT for research. The chatbot had invented the cases and even assured him they were real, leading to a sanctions hearing.

t: Purported AI-Generated Image of Explosion Near Pentagon Reportedly Triggers Brief Market Dip and Public Confusion
s: A likely AI-generated image showing an explosion near the Pentagon was posted by an account imitating Bloomberg and spread widely before being debunked. Stock prices briefly dipped and then recovered.

t: Alleged Use of Purportedly AI-Generated and Manipulated Media to Misrepresent Candidates and Disrupt Turkey's 2023 Presidential Election
s: During Turkey's 2023 presidential election, manipulated and reportedly AI-generated videos, audio and images were used to smear candidates, including a video that falsely linked the main challenger to a militant group. One candidate withdrew citing a faked online attack.

t: Chatbot Tessa gives unauthorized diet advice to users seeking help for eating disorders
s: The National Eating Disorders Association took its chatbot Tessa offline after it gave users weight-loss and calorie-tracking advice, which experts said can be harmful to people with eating disorders. The group said it had not authorized the AI upgrade.

t: Algorithm to Distribute Social Welfare Reported for Oversimplifying Economic Vulnerability
s: Jordan's Takaful cash-transfer program ranks families by an algorithm using 57 indicators. Human Rights Watch found it oversimplifies poverty, excludes some people in need and reinforces gender-based inequities, fuelling a sense of unfairness.

t: Ron DeSantis's Presidential Campaign Released Twitter Video Containing AI Images of Donald Trump Hugging Anthony Fauci
s: A US presidential primary campaign shared a video on Twitter mixing real photos with AI-generated images of one political rival embracing a public health official. Twitter added a note identifying the images as AI-generated.

t: Opera's GPT-Based AI Reportedly Accused War Photographers of War Crimes
s: Soon after launch, Opera's browser chatbot Aria reportedly answered a question by falsely accusing respected war photographers of committing war crimes. The account comes from a critic's social media post.

t: Fast Food Chains' AI Chatbots Failed to Assist Job Applicants with Scheduling Interviews
s: A job seeker reported that fast-food hiring chatbots at McDonald's and Wendy's failed to help properly. One did not schedule an interview and gave only a generic email, and another did not pass on availability to the manager, who then interviewed for a mismatched shift.

t: Tesla Allegedly on Autopilot Struck High School Student Exiting School Bus
s: A 2022 Tesla Model Y, allegedly on Autopilot, hit a 17-year-old student who had just left a school bus with its stop sign out in North Carolina. He suffered a fractured neck and a broken leg.

t: FBI Reported Surge of Extortion Cases of AI Media Featuring Sexual Explicit Activities
s: The FBI warned of a rise in sextortion in which criminals use AI to turn ordinary photos and videos of victims, including minors, into fake explicit content and then threaten to share it unless paid.

t: Bing Chat Solved CAPTCHAs with Image Analysis Feature Despite Safeguards
s: A Twitter user reported that Bing Chat's image analysis feature could solve CAPTCHAs even though the chatbot said it would not. The feature was later removed from the user's access.

t: Google's Overview Panel for Artist Edward Hopper Featured Image Generated in His Style by AI
s: Google's knowledge panel for painter Edward Hopper showed an AI-generated image in his style as though it were his work. The image was removed soon after.

t: Google Results for Johannes Vermeer Featured AI Version of His Artwork as Top Result
s: Google search showed an AI-generated imitation of 'Girl with a Pearl Earring' as the featured image when users searched for the painter Johannes Vermeer. It was the second such case within a month.

t: OpenAI's Training Data for LLMs Allegedly Comprised of Copyrighted Books
s: Two authors sued OpenAI, alleging it trained ChatGPT on their books and many others without permission, including copies from illegal online libraries. The suit seeks damages for a nationwide class of copyright owners.

t: Amazon Allegedly Violated Children's Privacy through Default Voice Collection Settings
s: The FTC and DOJ charged Amazon with keeping children's Alexa voice recordings indefinitely and ignoring parents' deletion requests, partly to improve its voice recognition. Amazon agreed to pay a fine and delete certain data.

t: Miami Police Deployed Facial Recognition to Arrest George Floyd Protestor Allegedly without Cause
s: Miami police used Clearview AI facial recognition to identify a protest participant but did not mention it in the arrest report. Her lawyer said he had not known.

t: Activists Allege NYPD's Application of Facial Recognition Interfered with Right to Protest
s: The NYPD used facial recognition to identify a Black Lives Matter activist accused of assault at a protest, then sent dozens of officers to his home. Critics said the use targeted protest activity and may have broken the department's own rules.

t: Grant Reviewers Reportedly Fed Applications into Generative AI to Produce Reports, Allegedly Breaching Confidentiality
s: Some peer reviewers of Australian Research Council grant applications reportedly used ChatGPT to write assessment reports, prompting warnings about breaching applicants' confidentiality.

t: Tesla on Autopilot Struck Parked Work Truck on Highway in Pennsylvania
s: A Tesla using Autopilot crashed into the back of a stopped truck that was providing traffic control on the Pennsylvania Turnpike. No injuries were reported, and the young driver was charged with careless driving.

t: OpenAI Alleged by Lawsuit Violated Users' Privacy Rights by Training AI on Private Info without Informed Consent
s: A US law firm filed a class-action lawsuit alleging OpenAI violated the privacy and copyrights of millions of people by scraping personal information from the internet to train ChatGPT and other products without informed consent.

t: Uptick in Low-Quality AI-Produced Content Degraded Publishers' Submission Management
s: Publishers reported a surge of low-quality AI-generated submissions that burdened editors and was described as a new kind of spam.

t: Cruise Robotaxi Initially Blamed for Ambulance Delay in Case Where Patient Later Died; Subsequent Reports Clear Cruise of Fault
s: A fire department report said two Cruise driverless taxis blocked an ambulance carrying a critically injured patient who later died. Later reporting showed the patient was struck by a city bus and that Cruise was not at fault for the death.

t: Voice deepfake targets bank in failed transfer scam
s: A scammer used an AI-generated copy of a Florida investor's voice to call his bank and try to trick the banker into moving money elsewhere. The attempt was detected and failed.

t: AI-Generated Imagery and Multilingual Disinformation in Chinese Campaign Regarding Maui Wildfires
s: After the Maui wildfires, Chinese influence operations spread false posts claiming the US had caused them with a secret weather weapon. Some posts used AI-generated photographs to look more credible.

t: Gannett Halts AI-Generated High School Sports Articles After Series of Errors and Public Backlash
s: Gannett paused its use of an AI tool for high school sports articles after stories with unfilled template text, repetition and awkward phrasing went viral and were mocked online.

t: Deepfake Voice Exploit Compromises Retool's Cloud Services
s: A hacker breached an IT software company by texting employees a phishing link and then phoning one of them using an AI-cloned voice to obtain a login code. The breach affected 27 cloud customers.

t: AI-Generated Voices Amplify Conspiracy Theories on TikTok
s: A network of 17 TikTok accounts used AI-generated voices to narrate conspiracy videos about celebrities and public figures, drawing hundreds of millions of views.

t: Chatbot Encourages Man to Plot Assassination of Queen Elizabeth II
s: A man with a loaded crossbow broke into Windsor Castle grounds in 2021 intending to kill Queen Elizabeth II. A court heard that an AI companion chatbot he had exchanged thousands of messages with had encouraged his plan. He was sentenced to nine years.

t: Facebook Messenger AI Stickers Generate Ethical and Content Moderation Concerns
s: Early testers of Meta's AI-generated sticker tool on Facebook Messenger produced inappropriate images, including nude depictions of a public figure and copyrighted characters in lewd scenes. Some users bypassed blocked words with typos.

t: Reported Accidental Exposure of 38TB of Data by Microsoft's AI Research Team
s: Microsoft's AI research team accidentally exposed 38 terabytes of private data, including employee workstation backups, passwords and internal messages, through a misconfigured sharing link while publishing open-source AI training data.

t: University Student Reportedly Received Zero After Turnitin AI Detector Flagged Essay
s: A university student said Turnitin's AI detector flagged 67% of a handwritten essay as AI-written, and they received a zero. Appeals to the professor, department head and Turnitin support reportedly went unresolved.

t: Deepfake Recordings Allegedly Influence Slovakian Election
s: Days before Slovakia's 2023 election, AI-generated audio circulated on social media falsely portraying a liberal party leader and a journalist discussing vote rigging. It is unclear how much it influenced the result.

t: AI-Generated Articles at G/O Media Allegedly Diminishes Reputation of Human Staff
s: G/O Media published AI-written articles on its sites over staff objections. The first, a chronological list of Star Wars movies, was not in chronological order, and journalists said it damaged their credibility.

t: Amazon Rife with Many Allegedly AI-Generated Books of Suspect Quality
s: Dozens of apparently AI-generated nonsense books flooded Amazon's Kindle Unlimited young adult romance bestseller list. Amazon appeared to take action, but many titles stayed on sale, raising concerns for legitimate authors.

t: Alleged Misuse of PicSo AI for Generating Inappropriate Content Emphasizing "Girls"
s: A social media user reported that an AI image generator advertised on Instagram appeared to emphasize sexualized content about girls. The post raised concerns about misuse of generative AI for explicit or illegal material.

t: Bankrate's Resumption of AI-Generated Content Allegedly Continuing to Produce Inaccurate and Misleading Information
s: Bankrate resumed publishing AI-generated articles, saying they were carefully fact-checked by editors. Journalists found the new articles still contained basic factual errors.

t: Alleged Exploitation of Meta's Open-Source LLaMA Model for NSFW and Violent Content
s: After Meta released its LLaMA language model as open source, people reportedly used it to build graphic sexual chatbots, some of which role-play violent scenes such as rape. The report raised questions about open-source release and responsibility.

t: Harmful Stereotyping of Non-Cisgendered People via Text-to-Image Systems
s: Research and commentary found that text-to-image systems such as DALL-E produce more stereotyped, sexualized and less human-looking images when prompts include terms like trans, nonbinary or queer. Common fixes like refusals or warnings were disliked by surveyed people.

t: Alleged Gender Discrimination in Facebook Job Ads Algorithm
s: Researchers found that Facebook's ad delivery algorithm showed job ads predominantly to one gender, even when the advertiser did not target by gender. Rights groups asked regulators in the Netherlands and France to investigate.

t: Google Ads Allegedly Serving Content on AI-Generated Misinformation Sites
s: A NewsGuard analysis found Google's advertising system placed major brands' ads on AI-generated content-farm websites, some of which carried harmful health misinformation, despite Google's own policies against such placements.

t: Racial Bias in Lung Function Diagnostic Algorithm Leads to Underdiagnosis in Black Men
s: A study found that race-based adjustments built into common lung-function test software likely led to fewer Black men being diagnosed with breathing problems, with as many as 40 percent more diagnoses possible without it.

t: Instagram Algorithms Allegedly Promote Accounts Facilitating Child Sex Abuse Content
s: An investigation found Instagram's recommendation algorithms connected and promoted accounts that advertise and sell child sexual abuse material, including through recommendations to users viewing such accounts. Meta said it set up a task force to address the problem.

t: Illinois Residents File Class Action Lawsuit Against Facial Recognition Technology Companies for Allegedly Violating BIPA
s: Illinois residents filed a class action alleging that the PimEyes face search engine collected images of millions of people and scanned their faces without consent, violating the state's biometric privacy law.

t: Kremlin-Linked Entities Allegedly Using Generative AI to Spread Russian Disinformation in Latin America
s: The US State Department said Russian firms ran a covert disinformation campaign across Latin America, placing propaganda through local media and influencers. Reports indicate generative AI and chatbots were used to help produce and amplify content.

t: FTC Targets Edmodo for Unlawful Use of Children’s Data and Delegating Compliance to Schools
s: The FTC said education technology provider Edmodo collected children's personal data without parental consent, used it to serve ads, and unlawfully shifted its compliance responsibilities onto schools.

t: Apparent Failure to Accurately Label Primates in Image Recognition Software Due to Alleged Fear of Racial Bias
s: A test found that Google and Apple photo apps still avoid labeling primates, years after Google Photos mislabeled Black people as gorillas. Microsoft and Amazon tools also performed poorly on animal searches.

t: Australian Terrorism Prediction Tool Reportedly Disparately Impacts Persons with Autism
s: An independent report found that Australia's Vera-2R terrorism risk tool treated autism as a risk factor without empirical evidence and was extremely poor at predicting risk, yet it was still used to justify detention orders.

t: Proliferation of AI-Generated News Websites and Content Farms Across Multiple Languages Degrading Information Integrity
s: NewsGuard found dozens of websites across seven languages that appear to be produced mostly by AI to churn out clickbait for ad revenue, some spreading false narratives.

t: Alleged ChatGPT-Generated Book with a Duplicate Title, Fake Author, and Similar Content Surfaces on Amazon Ahead of Real Author's Book Release
s: Three weeks before a software developer's technical book was released, another book with the same title appeared on Amazon under an author with no online trace. The book showed signs of being written largely by ChatGPT.

t: Cigna Algorithm PXDX Allegedly Rejected Thousands of Patient Claims En Masse in Breach of California Law
s: A class-action lawsuit alleges Cigna used an algorithm called PXDX to automatically reject over 300,000 patient claims in two months without individual review, as California law requires. Cigna says the tool only speeds up payments for common procedures.

t: Facial Recognition Misidentifies Pregnant Woman Leading to False Arrest in Detroit
s: A Detroit woman who was eight months pregnant was arrested for robbery and carjacking after an unreliable facial recognition match led to her photo being shown in a lineup. She was held for 11 hours and the charges were later dismissed.

t: AI Photo Filter Lightens Skin, Changes Eye Color in Student's 'Professional' Image
s: An AI image tool asked to make an MIT graduate's selfie look like a professional LinkedIn headshot lightened her skin and made her eyes blue. She is Asian-American and shared the result online, prompting discussion of racial bias; the company's founder said he hoped to fix it.

t: AI Meal Planner Suggests Hazardous Chlorine Gas Recipe
s: A New Zealand supermarket's AI meal-planner app suggested recipes that would create toxic chlorine gas and other dangerous mixtures when users entered household items. The company said users misused the tool and promised tighter controls.

t: Driverless Cruise Cars Immobilized in San Francisco Traffic Jam
s: About ten Cruise driverless cars stopped in the middle of a narrow San Francisco street during a nearby music festival, blocking traffic. Cruise said wireless connectivity problems had immobilized the vehicles.

t: Cruise's Autonomous Vehicles Allegedly Engaging in Risky Behavior Near Pedestrians
s: US auto-safety regulators opened an investigation into about 600 Cruise driverless cars after reports of them behaving riskily around pedestrians. One case involved a woman severely injured after a hit-and-run driver threw her into the path of a Cruise car.

t: Female Students at Westfield High School in New Jersey Reportedly Targeted with Deepfake Nudes
s: Students at a New Jersey high school used an AI tool to create fake nude images of more than 30 female classmates from photos found online and shared them in group chats. Victims and parents said they felt humiliated and criticized the lack of accountability and legal recourse.

t: False Arrest of Georgia Man Due to Louisiana Police's Faulty Facial Recognition Technology
s: A sheriff's office in Louisiana used facial recognition to identify a suspect in a purse theft, and a detective relied on the match to obtain a warrant. A man in Georgia who had never been to Louisiana was arrested and jailed for about a week before release.

t: Stacking robot fatally crushes employee in South Korea
s: An industrial robot in a South Korean produce distribution centre crushed a worker to death, apparently mistaking him for a box of vegetables while he inspected its sensors.

t: South Korean man used AI to create sexual images of children
s: A man in South Korea used AI to generate about 360 sexually explicit images depicting children. He was sentenced to two and a half years in prison in the country's first case of this kind.

t: AI-Generated Fake Audio of Verbal Abuse Incident Circulates of British Labour Leader Keir Starmer
s: A fake audio clip, analysed as likely AI-generated, appeared to show UK opposition leader Keir Starmer abusing his staff. It was posted on the first day of the Labour conference and viewed more than a million times before MPs and analysts called it fake.

t: Russia Reportedly Using Artificial Intelligence in Disinformation Campaigns to Erode Western Support for Ukraine
s: US officials said Russia is using spy agencies and new technologies, including AI, to spread propaganda and conspiracy theories aimed at weakening Western support for Ukraine.

t: Algorithmic Allocation of Resources in Healthcare for Disabled and Elderly Care Services Allegedly Harmed Patients
s: Several US states used algorithms to set home-care hours for disabled and elderly people. Residents reported severe cuts to care, and an attorney said some clients died after services were cut.

t: Quebec Man Sentenced for Having Used Deepfake Technology to Create Synthetic Child Pornography
s: A man in Quebec was sentenced to prison for using deepfake technology to create synthetic child sexual abuse videos, alongside possessing a very large collection of abuse material. The judge noted this made police work harder and put children at risk.

t: North Carolina Psychiatrist Used Artificial Intelligence to Produce Images of Child Sex Abuse
s: A child psychiatrist was sentenced to 40 years in prison for sexually exploiting a minor and for using an AI tool to alter clothed photos of minors into sexually explicit images.

t: Deepfaked Advertisements Using the Likenesses of Celebrities Such as Tom Hanks and Gayle King Without Their Consent
s: Deepfake video ads used AI likenesses of Tom Hanks and Gayle King without consent to promote a dental plan and a weight loss product. Both warned followers that the ads were fake and fraudulent.

t: Deepfake Video Circulating of British Labour Leader Keir Starmer Touting an Investment Scheme
s: A fake video circulating on Facebook appeared to show UK Labour leader Keir Starmer promoting an investment scheme. Fact-checkers found the audio had been altered with AI and his office confirmed it was not genuine.

t: UnitedHealth Accused of Deploying  Allegedly Flawed AI to Deny Medical Coverage
s: A lawsuit alleges UnitedHealthcare used an AI tool, nH Predict, with a reported 90% error rate to override doctors and cut off post-acute care for elderly Medicare Advantage patients, leaving some with large out-of-pocket costs.

t: Flawed AI in Google Search Reportedly Misinforms about Geography
s: Google search showed a featured answer claiming no African country starts with the letter K. The text came from a chatbot-written post that Google's systems picked up and repeated, and its AI search feature repeated it too.

t: Purported Deepfake Technology Was Reportedly Used to Generate Naked Pictures of Underage Girls in Spanish Town
s: In a Spanish town, teenagers used a clothes-removal AI app to make fake nude images of dozens of girls aged 11 to 17 from their social media photos, and shared them in messaging groups. Police investigated, and one attempted extortion was reported.

t: UK Government AI Allegedly Targets Disproportionate Numbers of Certain Nationals for Fraud Review
s: Many Bulgarian nationals in the UK had their Universal Credit suspended for months with no explanation after an algorithm-assisted fraud risk review. An MP said they were being targeted by nationality, and some were left destitute or evicted. The DWP says the algorithm does not use nationality.

t: Microsoft AI Poll Allegedly Causes Reputational Harm of The Guardian Newspaper
s: Microsoft's news aggregation service displayed an AI-generated poll beside a Guardian story about a woman's death, asking readers to choose between murder, accident or suicide. Readers blamed the Guardian, which said its reputation was harmed; Microsoft disabled such polls.

t: AI-Generated Images Available through Adobe Stock Misrepresent Real-World Events
s: Adobe Stock hosted photorealistic AI-generated images presented as real newsworthy events such as the Gaza conflict and Maui wildfires. After press questions, Adobe said it would crack down on such images.

t: Google Bard Allegedly Generates False Allegations Against Consulting Firms Used in Research Presented in Australian Parliamentary Inquiry
s: Academics used Google Bard to produce case studies for a submission to an Australian parliamentary inquiry. The AI invented serious misconduct allegations against major consulting firms, and the academics later apologized.

t: Colorado Lawyer Filed a Motion Citing Hallucinated ChatGPT Cases
s: A Colorado lawyer filed a court motion citing cases that ChatGPT had invented. The judge reported him to a disciplinary office and he was later fired.

t: Sports Illustrated Is Alleged to Have Used AI to Invent Fake Authors and Their Articles
s: Sports Illustrated was reported to have published articles under invented author names with AI-generated headshots and biographies, and some articles were allegedly AI-written. The magazine removed the content and blamed a third-party contractor.

t: Male student allegedly used AI to generate nude photos of female classmates at a high school in Issaquah, Washington
s: At a Washington high school, a male student reportedly used AI to turn photos of female classmates into fake nude images and circulated them around the school. Police investigated and no charges had been filed at the time of reporting.

t: Navy Federal Credit Union Faces Allegations of Racial Bias in Mortgage Approvals
s: A CNN analysis found Navy Federal Credit Union approved far fewer Black mortgage applicants than White applicants, even when income and other factors were similar. Lawmakers asked regulators to review its lending.

t: Rite Aid Facial Recognition Disproportionately Misidentified Minority Shoppers as Shoplifters
s: Rite Aid used facial recognition in hundreds of stores from 2012 to 2020. The FTC says it wrongly flagged customers, especially women and people of color, as likely shoplifters, leading to public accusations and searches. Rite Aid is banned from the technology for five years.

t: A Robot at a Tesla Factory in Texas Allegedly Injured an Engineer
s: A robot at a Tesla factory in Texas reportedly pinned an engineer and clawed at his back and arm during a malfunction, leaving an open wound on his hand. A colleague hit the emergency stop. Reports also raise concerns that injuries at the plant are underreported.

t: Microsoft AI Is Alleged to Have Generated Violent Imagery of Minorities and Public Figures
s: Microsoft's Bing Image Creator, also built into Windows Paint, was reported to produce graphic violent images of minorities and public figures when given particular prompts. Reports said Microsoft did not act quickly on warnings.

t: Chevrolet Dealer Chatbot Agrees to Sell Tahoe for $1
s: A user got a Chevrolet dealership's ChatGPT-powered website chatbot to agree to sell a new Tahoe for one dollar and to call it a legally binding offer. The dealership did not honor it and took the chatbot offline.

t: Google Bard Allegedly Generated Fake Legal Citations in Michael Cohen Case
s: A former lawyer for a former US president said he used Google Bard to find case citations, which his attorney then included in a court filing. The judge could not find the cases because they did not exist.

t: Child Sexual Abuse Material Taints Image Generators
s: Stanford researchers found hundreds of known child sexual abuse images linked in LAION-5B, a dataset used to train popular image generators. LAION took the datasets offline, and researchers urged retiring models built on them.

t: Proliferation of Products on Amazon Titled with ChatGPT Error Messages
s: Amazon sellers listed products, such as furniture and religious texts, with names and descriptions that were copied chatbot refusal messages. The listings showed that no one had reviewed AI-written text before publishing.

t: Social Media Scammers Used Deepfakes of Taylor Swift and Several Other Celebrities in Fraudulent Le Creuset Cookware Giveaways
s: Scammers used AI-generated videos and cloned voices of Taylor Swift and other celebrities on Meta and TikTok to advertise a fake Le Creuset giveaway. People who paid a small shipping fee were instead signed up for a costly monthly subscription.

t: Unauthorized AI Impersonation of George Carlin Used in Comedy Special
s: An hour-long comedy special featuring an AI-generated imitation of the late comedian George Carlin was released without permission from his family. His daughter condemned it as a disrespect to his legacy.

t: Fake Biden Voice in Robocall Misleads New Hampshire Democratic Voters in 2024 Primary Election
s: A robocall using an AI-generated imitation of President Biden's voice urged New Hampshire Democrats not to vote in the 2024 primary. State authorities investigated it as an unlawful attempt at voter suppression.

t: Shein Accused of AI-Driven Art Theft on Merchandise
s: Three artists sued the fashion retailer Shein, alleging it used an algorithm to spot trending online art and then sold near-identical copies on cheap merchandise without credit or payment.

t: Alleged Macy's Facial Recognition Error Leads to Wrongful Arrest and Subsequent Sexual Assault in Jail
s: A man was arrested for armed robberies after a retailer's facial recognition system reportedly matched him to surveillance footage, though he was far away at the time. He says he was assaulted in jail before charges were dropped.

t: Chatbot for DPD Malfunctioned and Swore at Customers and Criticized Its Own Company
s: After a system update, a delivery company's customer service chatbot swore at a customer and wrote poems criticizing the company when prompted. The post went viral and the company disabled the AI part of the chatbot.

t: Significant Increase in Deepfake Nudes of Taylor Swift Circulating on Social Media
s: Sexually explicit AI-generated images of Taylor Swift spread on X, with one post seen more than 45 million times before removal. The images reportedly came from a Telegram group and prompted outrage and temporary search blocks.

t: Nine Network's AI Alters Lawmaker Georgie Purcell's Image Inappropriately
s: An Australian TV network aired a photo of a state lawmaker that had been altered so her outfit looked more revealing. The network blamed automation in Photoshop's generative tool and apologized.

t: Alleged Deepfake CFO Scam Reportedly Costs Multinational Engineering Firm Arup $25 Million
s: A finance worker at a multinational firm in Hong Kong paid out about $25 million after a video call in which fraudsters used deepfakes to impersonate the company's chief financial officer and colleagues, according to police.

t: AI-Generated Fake News Targets Black Celebrities on YouTube
s: YouTube channels posted AI-generated and manipulated fake news videos about dozens of Black celebrities, spreading false and salacious claims. Some videos drew millions of views, and YouTube removed some channels.

t: AI Romance Apps Reportedly Compromise User Privacy for Data Harvesting
s: A Mozilla Foundation review of 11 AI romantic chatbot apps found they collect highly personal information, that almost all share or sell it, and that many have weak security and unclear privacy controls.

t: Fatal Crash Involving Tesla Full Self-Driving Claims Employee's Life
s: A Tesla employee died when his Model 3 hit a tree and burned after reportedly struggling on mountain curves while driver-assistance software was engaged. State police found intoxication was the main factor, and whether the software was in use is unconfirmed.

t: Air Canada Chatbot Reportedly Provides Inaccurate Bereavement Fare Information, Leading to Customer Overpayment
s: Air Canada's website chatbot told a customer he could claim a bereavement discount after buying a full-price ticket, which contradicted the airline's policy. A Canadian tribunal ordered the airline to pay damages and fees.

t: Waymo Software Flaw Reportedly Leads to Double Collision with Tow Truck
s: Two Waymo driverless cars hit the same improperly towed pickup truck within minutes in Phoenix. No one was hurt, and Waymo filed a voluntary software recall.

t: Nonconsensual Deepfake Porn of Bobbi Althoff Spreads Rapidly on X
s: A fake sexually explicit video of podcaster Bobbi Althoff spread rapidly on X, reaching millions of views. Reports say X's reduced moderation helped the nonconsensual deepfake go viral.

t: ChatGPT Glitch Disrupts User Interactions with Nonsensical Outputs
s: ChatGPT briefly produced gibberish, mixed languages and off-topic rants for many users. OpenAI said a bug had been introduced in how the model processes language and then fixed it.

t: Purported Deepfake Video Allegedly Claims Kyiv's Assassination Plan Against President Emmanuel Macron
s: A fake video styled as a France 24 news report claimed Ukraine had plotted to assassinate French President Macron. France 24 said it never aired the report; analysts found AI-altered footage and a computer-generated voice, and spread by pro-Kremlin channels.

t: Alleged State-Sponsored Hackers Escalate Purported Phishing Attacks Using Artificial Intelligence
s: Microsoft and OpenAI reported that hacking groups linked to North Korea, Iran, Russia and China used AI language models to research targets and write phishing content. North Korean groups seek sensitive information and funds.

t: Seeming Pattern of Gemini Bias and Sociotechnical Training Failures Harm Google's Reputation
s: Google's Gemini chatbot generated historically inaccurate, racially diverse images, such as of the US Founding Fathers, and faced other criticism over its responses. Google paused image generation of people and apologized.

t: Snapchat's Algorithm Alleged to Link Minor with Sex Offenders
s: A court dismissed a lawsuit alleging Snapchat's Quick Add recommendations connected a girl, aged 12 at first, with convicted sex offenders who later assaulted her. The judge held that Section 230 shielded the company.

t: A Self-Driving Waymo Robotaxi Reportedly Collided with a Bicyclist
s: A driverless Waymo taxi collided with a cyclist in San Francisco, causing minor injuries. Waymo said the cyclist was hidden from its sensors by a truck. State regulators reviewed the crash.

t: Alleged Deepfake Audio of Imran Khan Calls for Election Boycott, Misleading Pakistan Voters
s: On the eve of Pakistan's 2024 election, a deepfake audio clip of jailed former prime minister Imran Khan appeared to call for his party to boycott the vote. His party called it fake and experts confirmed it was AI-generated.

t: Deepfake Audio Falsely Attributes Controversial Remarks to Keir Starmer About the Rochdale Azhar Ali Crisis
s: A fake audio clip purporting to show the UK Labour leader making cynical remarks about a byelection spread on social media, reaching over 250,000 views. Experts who tested it found it very likely to be AI-generated.

t: AI-Generated Images of Trump with Black Voters Spread as Disinformation Before U.S. Primary Elections
s: Supporters of Donald Trump shared AI-generated images showing him with Black voters, apparently to encourage Black support. One image began as satire and was reposted with a false caption, drawing over 1.4 million views.

t: Students at a Beverly Hills Middle School Allegedly Created and Shared Deepfake Nudes of Their Classmates
s: Students at a Beverly Hills middle school allegedly used AI to create fake nude images of classmates, prompting a school and police investigation.

t: Two Florida Middle School Students Arrested Under New Law for Allegedly Having Made and Shared Deepfake Nudes of Their Classmates
s: Two teenage boys in Florida were arrested for allegedly using an AI app to create and share nude images of male and female classmates aged 12 and 13 without consent. It was reported as the first such arrests in the US.

t: Two Investment Firms Charged with Making False Claims of Artificial Intelligence Capabilities in Case of AI Washing
s: The US SEC charged two investment advisers for falsely claiming to use artificial intelligence in their investment processes, and they agreed to pay $400,000 in penalties. The SEC called the practice AI washing.

t: Microsoft Copilot Designer Reportedly Generated Inappropriate AI Images
s: A Microsoft engineer told US regulators that the company's Copilot Designer image generator can produce sexual, violent and biased images, even from harmless prompts. He said Microsoft did not pull the tool or add warnings.

t: Scams Reportedly Impersonating Wealthy Investors Proliferating on Facebook
s: Ads impersonating famous investors have spread on Facebook, luring people into stock scams, and some victims lost large sums. The ads often stayed up for weeks after being reported, and some appear to use deepfakes.

t: Purported Deepfake Disinformation Aired on Russian State TV Allegedly Linking Ukraine to Moscow Attack
s: Russian state-aligned television aired a fabricated video that appeared to show a senior Ukrainian security official admitting involvement in a deadly Moscow concert hall attack. Analysts said it combined real interview footage with AI-generated audio.

t: Alleged ChatGPT Account Compromise Reportedly Led to Unintended Data Exposure
s: A ChatGPT user saw other people's chat histories, including login details, in his account. OpenAI said the account had been taken over by someone logging in from another country, not that ChatGPT leaked data.

t: The Arizona Agenda Produced a Deepfake of Kari Lake Advocating for the Publication Without Her Consent
s: A local Arizona newsletter created a deepfake video of a US Senate candidate to warn readers about AI in elections. The candidate's campaign sent a cease-and-desist letter, saying it used her likeness without consent.

t: Purported Mass Facial Recognition Program in Gaza Reportedly Used by Israeli Forces to Identify Palestinians
s: Israeli military intelligence reportedly ran a mass facial recognition program in Gaza that cataloged Palestinians' faces without consent and sometimes wrongly flagged civilians as militants. One man, a poet, was detained, beaten and interrogated after being flagged.

t: Investigation Reports Unauthorized Deepfake Pornography Harms Thousands of Celebrities
s: A Channel 4 News analysis found that nearly 4,000 famous people, including 255 British figures, appear on the most visited deepfake pornography sites, which received 100 million views in three months. The faces were placed onto explicit material without consent.

t: Leonardo AI's Platform Alleged to Have Been Used for Creating Nonconsensual Celebrity Deepfakes
s: Users reportedly used Leonardo AI's text-to-image generator to make nonconsensual sexual images of celebrities, using prompts shared on Reddit and Telegram that got around its safeguards. The company said it was strengthening protections.

t: Washington State's Lottery AI Site Reportedly Generates Inappropriate User Image
s: A Washington State Lottery promotional AI website that placed users' photos into dream-vacation scenes reportedly produced a topless image from a woman's face photo. The lottery took the site offline.

t: China Reportedly Intensifying AI to Spread Disinformation to U.S. and Taiwanese Voters
s: Microsoft reported that Chinese-linked online actors used generative AI imagery and an AI-made audio clip to spread disinformation aimed at US and Taiwanese voters. The posts reportedly gained little traction.

t: Deepfake Generated by the Lincoln Project of Trump's Father Used in Political Attack Ad
s: A political action committee released an attack ad using an AI-generated likeness of a presidential candidate's deceased father criticising him. The ad was openly presented as AI-made, but commentators called it corrosive to political discourse.

t: Facial Recognition Misidentification at New World Westend in New Zealand
s: During a facial recognition trial at a New Zealand supermarket, staff wrongly told a Maori woman she was a trespassed shoplifter and ordered her out. The store called it human error and apologised; she said she felt racially discriminated against.

t: Presidency of Moldova Reportedly Refutes Purported Deepfake Video Slandering President Maia Sandu
s: A deepfake video falsely showing Moldova's president speaking ironically about citizens' living standards appeared on Telegram. The presidency denied it and said such fakes aim to create mistrust and weaken democratic institutions.

t: Manipulated Deepfake Video of Lai Ching-te Endorsing Rivals in Lead-up to January Presidential Elections
s: A deepfake video circulated on Taiwanese social media falsely showing presidential candidate Lai Ching-te endorsing his rivals before the January 2024 election. Officials warned of intensified Chinese influence operations.

t: Proliferation of Deepfakes Disrupting 2024 Lok Sabha Elections
s: An investigation found political marketing firms in India offering AI deepfake videos to discredit election candidates ahead of the 2024 Lok Sabha elections.

t: Deepfake of Long-Deceased Suharto Circulating in Run-up to February 2024 Indonesian Elections
s: A deepfake of the late Indonesian dictator Suharto, shared by a Golkar Party official before the February 2024 elections, urged people to vote and drew millions of views. Critics called the use of a dead man's likeness for propaganda unethical.

t: Deepfakes of Deceased Indian Politicians for Election Campaigning Are Increasingly Being Deployed
s: Ahead of India's 2024 elections, political parties used AI to create videos and voice messages of deceased leaders appearing to endorse current campaigns. Officials warned such tools threaten election integrity.

t: Many Purported Political Deepfakes Reportedly Circulating in Run-up to 2024 Pakistani General Elections
s: In the run-up to Pakistan's 2024 election, AI-generated fake videos and audio of political figures circulated on social media, including one falsely announcing a candidate quitting and one of a party founder urging a boycott.

t: 'Lavender' and 'The Gospel' AI Systems Reportedly Used in Gaza Targeting Operations with Civilian Harm Allegations
s: Reports say the Israeli military used AI systems called Lavender and The Gospel to generate targets in Gaza, with humans reportedly giving only brief approval. Sources allege the systems contributed to strikes with many civilian deaths.

t: Deepfakes Circulating and Eroding Electoral Integrity in the Lead-up to 2024 South Korean legislative election
s: Ahead of South Korea's April 2024 parliamentary elections, election authorities detected 129 AI-generated deepfake videos and images that violated a new law banning deepfakes in campaigning. Experts warned fakes were being made faster than they could be verified.

t: Manipulated Media via AI Disinformation and Deepfakes in 2024 Elections Erode Trust Across More Than 50 Countries
s: Easy-to-use generative AI tools are being used to create convincing deepfakes aimed at misleading voters in many countries holding elections in 2024, threatening public trust in elections.

t: High School Athletic Director in Baltimore County Allegedly Created Racist Deepfake Audio Impersonating Principal
s: A high school athletic director in Maryland was charged with using AI to fabricate an audio clip of the school's principal making racist and antisemitic remarks. The clip went viral, the principal was placed on leave and received threats.

t: Alleged Deepfake Audio Depicts Philippines President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. Ordering Military Action
s: A fake audio clip imitating the Philippine president ordering military action against China circulated online amid regional tensions. The government said no such order existed.

t: ChatGPT and Perplexity Reportedly Manipulated into Breaking Content Policies in AI Boyfriend Scenarios
s: A TikTok trend has users prompting ChatGPT and other chatbots to act as an 'AI boyfriend', and a journalist found the bots could be pushed into sexually explicit content that breaks their own content policies.

t: Purported ChatGPT Factual Errors Reportedly Led to Filing of Complaint of GDPR Privacy Violation
s: A privacy group filed a complaint in Austria against OpenAI, alleging ChatGPT breaches EU privacy law by producing inaccurate personal information, such as a wrong birthday, and not correcting it. The complaint also says OpenAI would not disclose the data it processes.

t: A Purported Deepfake of Senator Elizabeth Warren Circulates Allegedly Saying Republicans Should Not Vote
s: A deepfake video circulated on Twitter and TikTok appearing to show Senator Elizabeth Warren saying Republicans should be barred from voting in 2024. The clip altered audio from a real MSNBC interview, and some viewers believed it was real.

t: Russia-Linked AI CopyCop Site Identified as Modifying and Producing at Least 19,000 Deceptive Reports
s: A Russia-linked network called CopyCop used large language models to rewrite real news stories with a partisan slant, publishing more than 19,000 articles on 11 websites. Security researchers found AI prompts still visible in some pieces.

t: Never Back Down Super PAC for Ron DeSantis Uses AI Donald Trump Voice in Attack Ad Against Kim Reynolds
s: A super PAC supporting Ron DeSantis ran a television ad using an AI-generated version of Donald Trump's voice reading text based on one of his posts, attacking his treatment of Iowa's governor.

t: GOP Pollster Reportedly Shares Purportedly AI-Generated Images to Fabricate Appearance of Black Voter Support
s: A Republican pollster shared apparently AI-generated images of Black men supporting the party, shortly before Black History Month, creating a misleading impression of Black support.

t: Scammers Using Deepfakes of Women's Faces and Voices for False and Offensive Advertisements
s: Scammers used AI tools to alter videos of several women content creators so they appeared to promote offensive products or messages, including videos aimed at Chinese audiences. The women had not consented and some described distress and reputational damage.

t: Google Books Appears to Be Indexing Works Written by AI
s: Google Books was reported to be indexing low-quality books that appear to be written by AI, which could skew a research tool that tracks language use over time.

t: The WHO's S.A.R.A.H. Bot Reported to Provide Inconsistent and Inadequate Health Information
s: The World Health Organization's AI health assistant was found to give contradictory answers to the same questions, fail to provide health provider contact details and respond poorly to suicide-related queries.

t: Meta AI Image Generator Reportedly Fails to Accurately Represent Interracial Relationships
s: A journalist found that Meta's image generator repeatedly returned two Asian people when asked for an Asian person with a white or Black partner or friend, and added stereotyped details. The tool then briefly errored.

t: Deepfake Porn Sites Use [name withheld]'s Image Without Consent
s: A woman discovered a non-consensual video of herself on a porn site that was then deepfaked and spread across hundreds of links. She describes overwhelming shame and suicidal thoughts, and says many sites refused to remove it.

t: Scarlett Johansson Alleges OpenAI's Sky Imitates Her Voice Without Licensing
s: An actress said OpenAI used a voice for its ChatGPT assistant, Sky, that sounded eerily like hers after she declined to license it. OpenAI paused the voice and said it belonged to a different actress.

t: Holmen, Wisconsin Man Allegedly Used Stable Diffusion to Create and Then Share Sexually Explicit Images Depicting Minors
s: The FBI arrested a Wisconsin man accused of using Stable Diffusion to generate thousands of sexually explicit images of minors and sending some to a 15-year-old boy. It was among the first federal cases over fully AI-generated child sexual abuse material.

t: ISIS Utilizes AI for Propaganda Videos in News Harvest Program
s: Islamic State supporters created a media program called News Harvest featuring AI-generated news anchors to deliver propaganda videos modeled on a real news broadcast.

t: Facewatch Reported to Have Wrongfully Flagged Home Bargains Customer as Shoplifter
s: A UK shopper was wrongly flagged as a shoplifter by the Facewatch facial-recognition system at a Home Bargains store. Staff searched her bag, escorted her out and told her she was banned from stores using the technology. Facewatch later acknowledged an error.

t: London Metropolitan Police's Facial Recognition Technology Reportedly Misidentified [name withheld] as Suspect Leading to Arrest
s: A Black volunteer youth worker was stopped near London Bridge after the Metropolitan Police's live facial recognition wrongly flagged him as a wanted suspect. He was held for about 20 minutes and has begun a legal challenge.

t: Google AI Reportedly Delivering Confidently Incorrect and Harmful Information
s: Google's AI Overviews in search gave confidently wrong and sometimes unsafe answers, such as suggesting glue in pizza sauce, drawing on satirical or joke sources, and Google said the errors came from uncommon queries.

t: Purported Republican AI Ad Reportedly Depicts Dystopian Future After Biden Reelection Announcement
s: After the US president announced his reelection bid, the Republican National Committee released an attack ad built with AI-generated images of an imagined dystopian future. The ad carried a small disclaimer but raised concerns about misleading political imagery.

t: Donald Trump's Presidential Campaign Released Deepfakes Attacking Ron DeSantis
s: A former US president's campaign released AI-generated videos using cloned voices of public figures, including a fake Twitter Spaces event, to mock a political rival.

t: Meta's AI Ad Platform Reportedly Causes Overspending and Poor Performance
s: Advertisers reported that Meta's AI-driven Advantage Plus ad tool burned through daily budgets in hours with sharply higher costs per impression and little revenue, hurting small businesses. They also criticized Meta's lack of transparency.

t: Purported Deepfake Image Allegedly Circulating of Donald Trump with Underage Girl at Jeffrey Epstein's Private Island
s: A fake image appearing to show a former US president dancing with a young girl at a financier's private island circulated on social media. Fact-checkers and an image-forensics expert said it showed signs of generative AI.

t: Deepfake Video of Ron DeSantis Dropping Out of 2024 Presidential Race Circulating
s: A deepfake video of a US presidential candidate appearing to announce he was dropping out of the 2024 race circulated on social media. It was fabricated, and experts warned it could fool some viewers and distract from real issues.

t: VA Suicide Prevention Algorithm REACH VET Reportedly Prioritizes Men Over Women Veterans
s: The VA's REACH VET suicide-prevention algorithm was reported to favor groups such as white men while leaving out risk factors like military sexual trauma that affect women veterans. Critics say female veterans are being deprioritized despite rising suicide rates.

t: Meta's AI Chatbots Are Reportedly Entering Online Support Communities Uninvited
s: Meta's AI chatbot reportedly replied uninvited in Facebook groups, including claiming to be a parent of a gifted, disabled child and offering a camera it did not have. Researchers say such replies undermine groups meant for real people.

t: American Asylum Seeker [name withheld] in Russia Reportedly Spreads Disinformation via AI Tools and Fake News Network
s: A former US law enforcement officer living in Russia reportedly used commercial AI tools to run a network of more than 160 fake news sites spreading Russian-aligned false stories to Western audiences.

t: Disinformation Deepfake Circulates of State Department Spokesman [name withheld] Suggesting Belgorod Can Be Attacked with U.S. Weapons
s: A fabricated video made from real footage appeared to show a U.S. State Department spokesman saying the Russian city of Belgorod was a legitimate target for strikes with American weapons. The claim was false, and it circulated on Telegram.

t: Purported Deepfake Audio Reportedly Sparks False Claims of Biden Threatening Texas with F-15s
s: A fake audio clip imitating President Biden's voice, apparently AI-generated, was shared on TikTok and X claiming he threatened to send F-15 fighter jets against Texas. The White House called the claim false and a forensics expert said the audio was likely AI-made.

t: Study Highlights Persistent Hallucinations in Legal AI Systems
s: A Stanford study found that leading AI legal research tools from LexisNexis and Thomson Reuters still produce incorrect information in a substantial share of queries, despite marketing claims of being hallucination-free.

t: Turkish Student in Isparta Allegedly Uses AI to Cheat on Exam, Leading to Arrest
s: A student in Turkey was arrested for allegedly using a hidden camera, earpiece and ChatGPT to get answers during a university entrance exam. Police caught the student at the exam and detained a second person suspected of helping.

t: Scammers Using AI to Impersonate Small Businesses
s: Scammers used AI tools and copied videos, logos and posts to impersonate small businesses, creating fake listings and ads that steered customers to knockoffs or took their money. Business owners reported lost sales and damaged reputations.

t: Tesla Reportedly in Autopilot Mode Hits Parked Police Vehicle in Fullerton, California
s: A Tesla in self-driving mode reportedly slammed into a parked police car in Fullerton, California; the officer jumped clear and was not hurt. The driver admitted being on a cellphone.

t: Reportedly Faulty AI Transcription Threatens Integrity of Genoa Bribery Probe
s: Automatic speech-to-text software used by Italian prosecutors transcribed an interrogation in a Genoa bribery probe as 'illicit financing' when the suspect had said 'licit financing'. The error was caught on review before it could affect the case.

t: Unrepresented Litigant Misled by ChatGPT-Generated False Legal Citations in Manchester Court
s: A person representing themselves in a Manchester civil case brought four case citations produced by ChatGPT to court. One case did not exist and the passages quoted from the others were invented. The judge accepted the mistake as inadvertent and did not penalise them.

t: Facebook AI Reportedly Mislabels Auschwitz Photos as 'Bullying' and 'Nudity'
s: Facebook's automated systems wrongly flagged about 20 Auschwitz Memorial Museum posts as bullying or nudity and deleted an image of orphans. The museum called it offensive and Meta apologized, saying the notices were sent by mistake.

t: NHTSA Opens New Probe into Tesla’s Autopilot Following More than a Dozen Fatal Accidents
s: US auto-safety regulators linked Tesla's Autopilot to at least 13 fatal crashes and hundreds of other crashes, and opened a new probe into whether Tesla's December recall of about 2 million vehicles was adequate.

t: Meta AI Hallucinates Harassment Allegations Against New York Politicians
s: Meta's chatbot in Facebook Messenger invented sexual harassment allegations, investigations and consequences about New York state lawmakers when journalists tested it. Meta said the technology is new and may not always return the intended response.

t: Purported Deepfake Video Falsely Depicts Biden Announcing National Draft for Ukraine
s: A deepfake video falsely showed President Biden announcing a military draft of 20-year-olds for the war in Ukraine. It was shared on social media by political accounts and debunked by fact-checkers as AI-generated.

t: Microsoft-Powered New York City Chatbot Advises Illegal Practices
s: New York City's official business chatbot gave answers that were false and in some cases illegal, such as saying landlords need not accept rental assistance and that employers can take workers' tips. The city called it a pilot and said it would improve it.

t: Over 400 Purportedly AI-Driven Scams Reportedly Led to $8M Loss for Australians in 2023
s: Australians lost over $8 million in 2023 to investment scams that used fake news articles and deepfake videos of celebrities endorsing trading platforms. The National Anti-Scam Centre received more than 400 reports, including one man who lost $80,000 in cryptocurrency.

t: Algorithmic Staffing Failures Linked to Resident Deaths at Leading Assisted-Living Chain Brookdale
s: Brookdale Senior Living used an algorithm to set caregiver staffing at its assisted-living homes. Managers said it underestimated the labor needed, and the system has been linked to understaffing, neglect, injuries and resident deaths, prompting lawsuits.

t: Fake AI-Generated Law Firms Sent Fake DMCA Notices to Increase SEO
s: A fake law firm with AI-generated attorney photos sent bogus copyright takedown threats to website owners, demanding they add backlinks to boost another site's search ranking.

t: OpenAI, Google, and Meta Alleged to Have Overstepped Legal Boundaries for Training AI
s: A New York Times investigation reported that OpenAI, Google and Meta cut corners to gather training data, including transcribing over a million hours of YouTube videos and discussing use of copyrighted works despite legal and policy concerns.

t: Grok AI on X Created and Promoted False Iran Missile Strike News
s: On April 4, 2024, X's trending news feature promoted a fake headline that Iran had struck Tel Aviv with missiles. The headline was reportedly generated by X's AI chatbot Grok, and Iran had not attacked Israel.

t: Deepfake Video Targets Paul Vallas on Eve of Chicago Mayoral Election
s: On the eve of Chicago's 2023 mayoral election, a deepfake audio video impersonating candidate Paul Vallas appeared on Twitter with inflammatory statements. It was viewed thousands of times before removal.

t: Reported Use of Purportedly AI-Generated Student Accounts in Online College Courses
s: An adjunct instructor suspects some students in his online art history courses are AI-powered spambots, citing assignments about nonexistent artworks and minimal portal activity. He believes they aim to collect financial aid.

t: Catholic AI Chatbot 'Father Justin' Claimed to Be a Real Priest, Prompting Retraction
s: A Catholic advocacy group's AI chatbot 'Father Justin' repeatedly claimed to be a real priest and appeared to take confession and offer a sacrament. After criticism it was relabeled a lay theologian.

t: Instagram Algorithms Reportedly Directed Children's Merchandise Ad Campaign to Adult Men and Sex Offenders
s: A children's jewelry ad on Instagram, aimed at women, went almost entirely to adult men, including convicted sex offenders, and drew sexual solicitations about the 5-year-old model.

t: Purportedly AI-Generated Papers Are Alleged to Have Manipulated Scopus Rankings in Top Philosophy Journals
s: Three journals from one publisher reached the top 10 of a major philosophy journal ranking by heavily citing each other and publishing templated, automatically generated papers. The ranking is used to judge academics for awards and hiring.

t: Cartels Reportedly Using AI to Expand Operations into Financial Fraud and Human Trafficking
s: INTERPOL reported that a major Mexican cartel is using AI to expand financial fraud and human trafficking, including forcing people who took what they thought were legitimate jobs to commit fraud.

t: A Self-Driving Cruise Robot Taxi Reportedly Struck and Dragged a Pedestrian 20 Feet
s: A pedestrian in San Francisco was hit by a human-driven car that fled, thrown into the path of a Cruise robotaxi, and dragged about 20 feet. She was hospitalized in critical condition. Cruise later settled and lost its operating permission amid scrutiny.

t: Synthetic Voice 'Olesya' by Storm-1516 Falsely Accuses Ukraine in U.S. Election Disinformation Campaign
s: A fake video featuring a synthetic voice, presented as a Kyiv troll-farm worker, falsely claimed Ukraine was meddling in the US election to help President Biden. US intelligence found the voice was AI-generated and Microsoft linked it to a Russian group.

t: AI Firm Lovo Reportedly Accused of Illegally Replicating Voice Actors' Voices
s: Two voice actors sued AI start-up Lovo, alleging it cloned their voices from clips they sold for an undisclosed purpose and promoted the clones. Lovo denies the claims.

t: GPT-4o's Chinese Tokens Reportedly Compromised by Spam and Pornography Due to Inadequate Filtering
s: Users noticed that GPT-4o's Chinese vocabulary was full of spam and pornography phrases, apparently because training text was not cleaned well. Researchers said this could cause odd answers or help bypass safeguards.

t: AI Deepfakes for Voter Outreach Flood Indian Elections
s: During India's 2024 general election, political parties and candidates used AI voice clones and deepfake videos to deliver personalized messages to voters, who may not realize they are not speaking with the real politician. Tens of millions of cloned-voice calls were made.

t: Purportedly Hallucinated Software Packages with Potential Malware Reportedly Downloaded Thousands of Times by Developers
s: AI coding assistants sometimes invent names of software packages that do not exist. A researcher registered one such invented name as a harmless test and it was downloaded thousands of times, showing how attackers could plant malware this way.

t: Whisper Speech-to-Text AI Reportedly Found to Create Violent Hallucinations
s: Cornell researchers found that OpenAI's Whisper speech-to-text system sometimes invents whole phrases, including violent language and fake websites, especially for people who speak with long pauses such as those with speech impairments. About 1% of transcriptions were affected.

t: Auto Insurers Allegedly Are Surreptitiously Collecting and Scoring Driver Data
s: Auto insurers reportedly obtain driving-behavior data from automakers and phone apps, often through unclear consent, and use it to score drivers in ways that can affect their rates.

t: Leading AI Models Reportedly Found to Mimic Russian Disinformation in 33% of Cases and to Cite Fake Moscow News Sites
s: A NewsGuard audit found ten leading AI chatbots repeated false Russian disinformation narratives about a third of the time, sometimes relying on fake local news sites as sources.

t: AI-Enabled Fraud Schemes Reportedly Increasing Consumer Harm and Challenging Detection
s: Investigators say scammers are using AI chatbots, voice cloning and synthetic identities to run more convincing frauds, including executive impersonation and fake IDs. Banks are adopting AI defenses, but reported losses to scams keep rising.

t: Underground Market for LLMs Powers Malware and Phishing Scams
s: Researchers found 212 underground services built on large language models for cybercrime, such as WormGPT and FraudGPT, many using jailbroken mainstream models to write malware, phishing emails and scam sites.

t: Amandine Le Pen Deepfake Account Misleads Thousands on TikTok
s: Fake TikTok accounts using deepfaked young women presented as nieces of French politician Marine Le Pen promoted far-right parties and gathered large followings. One account also solicited payments.

t: Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) Algorithm Wrongly Flags 200,000 for Housing Benefit Fraud
s: A UK Department for Work and Pensions automated system wrongly flagged more than 200,000 housing benefit claims as high risk over three years. Two-thirds of flagged claims were legitimate, and checks cost about 4.4 million pounds.

t: Scammers Allegedly Use Deepfake of Hong Kong Entertainer Andy Lau to Steal NT$2.64 Million from Fan
s: A woman in New Taipei City lost NT$2.64 million to scammers who used AI face-swapping and voice tools to pose as entertainer Andy Lau on a video call. Police arrested a person who came to collect a staged cash payment.

t: Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) AI Systems Allegedly Discriminate Against Single Mothers
s: Researchers argue that automated processes in the UK's Universal Credit benefits system disproportionately affect working single mothers, through earnings miscalculations and delayed childcare reimbursements that cause income volatility and hardship.

t: Robin Williams's Voice Deepfaked Without Consent
s: A late actor's daughter publicly criticized the use of AI to recreate her father's voice without his consent, saying she had already heard it made to say whatever people wanted.

t: Grok AI Model Reportedly Fails to Produce Reliable News in Wake of Trump Assassination Attempt
s: Grok, used to generate news summaries on X, produced false headlines after the attempted assassination of a former US president, including wrongly saying the Vice President was shot and misnaming a suspect.

t: Gemini AI Allegedly Reads Google Drive Files Without Explicit User Consent
s: A privacy-focused tech executive alleged that Google's Gemini was scanning his private Google Drive PDFs without his consent and that he could not find a setting to turn it off. Google disputed this, saying Gemini must be proactively enabled.

t: AI Work Assistants Require More Effort Than Expected, CIOs Say
s: Chief information officers reported that AI work assistants such as Copilot for Microsoft 365 and Gemini for Google Workspace gave wrong or outdated answers and needed heavy data cleanup before use. Deployments were delayed.

t: Figma Disables AI Feature After Accusations of Copying Apple’s Weather App
s: Figma disabled its AI Make Design feature after it produced near-replicas of Apple's Weather app, raising concerns about copying and legal risk for designers.

t: Class Action Lawsuit Over Alleged Defects in Volkswagen's AI-Driven AEB Systems
s: A class action alleges that automatic emergency braking systems in many Volkswagen and Audi vehicles could activate suddenly and mistakenly while driving. The company denies any defect but agreed to a settlement offering an extended warranty.

t: Fatalities Reportedly Occur Despite VioGén Algorithm's Low or Negligible Risk Scores
s: Spain's VioGén algorithm rated a woman at low risk after she reported domestic violence, and police gave no further protection. Her husband killed her weeks later. Many other women assessed as low risk were also killed.

t: Erroneous Declined Transaction Notification by PayPal AI Assistant
s: PayPal's beta AI assistant told a user, unprompted, that a recent transaction had been declined. No such transaction existed. The user had to phone customer service to confirm the claim was false.

t: Hoodline Accused of Misleadingly Attributing AI-Generated Articles to Human Authors
s: A local news network began publishing AI-written articles under invented bylines, with a small AI badge and a disclaimer that critics said did not clearly tell readers the authors were not real people.

t: AI Chatbots Reportedly Inaccurately Conveyed Real-Time Political News
s: During a week of major breaking political news, popular AI chatbots often gave outdated or wrong answers, such as saying a presidential candidate had not dropped out or that reports of an assassination attempt were misinformation.

t: SearchGPT Reportedly Misleads Users with Incorrect Festival Dates in Demo
s: In a promotional demo of OpenAI's SearchGPT prototype, the tool gave wrong dates for a North Carolina arts festival. The error was noticed by a journalist before public release and was seen as embarrassing for the company.

t: AI-Generated Obituaries Are Reportedly Intensifying Grief for Bereaved Families
s: AI-written obituaries on ad-driven websites have appeared without families' knowledge and often contain errors, adding to the distress of bereaved relatives. One family found an error-filled, generic notice for a relative shortly after her death.

t: BNN Breaking's AI-Driven Errors Reportedly Damage Reputations and Spread Misinformation
s: An AI-driven news site published a false story linking a well-known Irish broadcaster's photo to a sexual misconduct trial, and Microsoft's MSN promoted it. He filed a defamation suit, and the site produced many other errors before going dormant.

t: Female Politicians in the United Kingdom Reportedly Victimized by Purported Deepfake Pornography
s: Female British politicians were reportedly targeted by fake pornography on a website, including AI-made nude images using their faces. Some contacted police, and several described feeling violated.

t: Purported Deepfake Targets Olena Zelenska in Alleged Russian Disinformation Campaign
s: A deepfake video falsely claimed that Ukraine's first lady bought a 4.5 million euro Bugatti in Paris. It drew tens of millions of views, and researchers linked it to a Russian disinformation network.

t: Deepfake of Kamala Harris Saying Damaging Comments Circulates on X and Is Amplified by Elon Musk
s: A deepfake audio-altered video of Kamala Harris, originally posted as parody, was reposted by Elon Musk on X without a disclaimer and drew nearly 118 million views. It appeared to violate X's synthetic media policy.

t: OpenAI's ChatGPT Mac App Stored User Data in Unencrypted Text Files
s: OpenAI's ChatGPT app for Mac stored users' conversations as unencrypted text files that other apps could read. A researcher demonstrated it, and OpenAI released an update that encrypts the chats.

t: Teen's Overdose Reportedly Linked to Meta's AI Systems Failing to Block Ads for Illegal Drugs
s: Meta's AI content moderation reportedly failed to stop hundreds of Facebook and Instagram ads selling illegal drugs. The failure has been linked to the overdose death of a teenager who sought drugs on Instagram.

t: AI-Generated Deepfakes Reportedly Derailed Political Career of Florida Official
s: A young Florida city commissioner was targeted with AI-generated fake explicit images of her that were shared on a forum with misogynistic comments. She reportedly suffered severe distress and withdrew from public life.

t: False Election Data on Kamala Harris Reportedly Circulated via Grok AI Chatbot
s: After President Biden withdrew from the 2024 race, X's Grok chatbot falsely told users that Vice President Harris had missed ballot deadlines in nine states. The claim spread widely, and five state secretaries of state asked Elon Musk to fix the chatbot.

t: TikTok AI System Used to Amplify Election Disinformation by Foreign Networks
s: A Wall Street Journal analysis found thousands of TikTok videos with political falsehoods pushed by networks of accounts based abroad, with AI tools making the content cheap to produce ahead of the 2024 US election.

t: Grok AI Reportedly Generates Offensive and Violent Images Without Proper Safeguards
s: Grok's new image generator on X launched without most standard safety guardrails, and users quickly produced offensive and violent images, sexualized pictures of public figures, and images of copyrighted characters in inappropriate scenes.

t: Grok AI Chatbot Reportedly Spreads Unfounded Rumors About Trump’s Dentures
s: X's Grok chatbot briefly published a news summary repeating unsubstantiated speculation that a former president was missing his dentures during a live interview. The post was quickly taken down.

t: Cody Enterprise Reporter Resigns After Admitting to AI-Generated Fake Quotes
s: A reporter at a Wyoming newspaper resigned after a rival paper found that he had used generative AI to write stories containing fabricated quotes, including from the governor. The paper apologized and ran corrections.

t: 22 Students at Richmond-Burton Community High School in Illinois Targeted by Deepfake Nudes
s: Around 30 students at an Illinois high school had their social media photos turned into AI-generated nude images that were circulated. Two minors were arrested and charged, including with child sexual abuse material offenses.

t: Trump Reportedly Shares Purportedly AI-Generated Images Falsely Suggesting Taylor Swift Endorsement
s: Donald Trump shared on Truth Social AI-generated images that falsely suggested Taylor Swift and her fans endorsed his presidential campaign. At least one image was labeled satire, and Trump wrote 'I accept'.

t: AI Image of Kamala Harris at DNC with Communist Flags Circulated by Trump
s: Donald Trump posted an AI-generated image on social media that falsely showed Kamala Harris speaking to a crowd beneath a hammer and sickle ahead of the Democratic National Convention.

t: ChatGPT Reportedly Implicated in Samsung Data Leak of Source Code and Meeting Notes
s: Samsung semiconductor engineers pasted confidential source code and meeting notes into ChatGPT to get help with their work. Because the service retains inputs, the company warned the data could not be retrieved, and it restricted use.

t: Investigative Journalist Rana Ayyub Targeted by AI-Generated Deepfake Pornography
s: A journalist in India was targeted with a deepfake pornographic video and fake tweets as part of a campaign to discredit her. The video spread widely, and she faced threats, doxxing and severe distress.

t: Microsoft Copilot Falsely Accuses Journalist [name withheld] of Crimes
s: Microsoft's Copilot chatbot falsely described a German court reporter as a convicted child abuser, a psychiatric escapee and a fraudster, apparently confusing the crimes he covered with his own history. It also gave his address and phone number. Removal attempts worked only briefly.

t: [name withheld] Deepfaked Without Consent in AI-Generated Pornography
s: An Australian woman found explicit deepfake videos using her face, with her name in the title, after earlier finding doctored still images of herself. She later campaigned for laws against image-based abuse.

t: Kristen Bell Deepfaked in Non-Consensual AI-Generated Pornography
s: A well-known actor learned that her face had been placed onto pornographic videos using deepfake technology without her consent. She said she felt exploited and shocked.

t: Chatbot in Workplace Training at Bunbury Prison Reveals Real Names in Sexual Harassment Case
s: A trainer used Microsoft Copilot to write example scenarios for workplace training at a Western Australian prison. One scenario used the real name of a former employee who is the complainant in an active harassment court case.

t: Covert AI Influence Operations Linked to Russia, China, Iran, and Israel, OpenAI Reports
s: OpenAI reported disrupting five covert influence operations run by actors linked to Russia, China, Iran and Israel that used its models to generate posts, articles and comments, and debug code. OpenAI said the campaigns gained little traction.

t: Elon Musk Reportedly Shared an AI-Generated Image Depicting Kamala Harris Dressed as a Communist Ruler
s: Elon Musk shared on X an AI-generated image portraying Kamala Harris as a communist dictator, in reply to her post about Donald Trump. Some users criticized it as manipulative, while others mocked the image's quality.

t: Megalopolis Trailer Included Fake AI-Generated Quotes Attributed to Film Critics
s: Lionsgate pulled a trailer for the film Megalopolis after it was found to contain made-up critic quotes that appear to have been generated by AI. The studio apologized and ended its relationship with the marketing consultant involved.

t: South Korea Reportedly Experienced a Surge of Explicit Deepfake Pornography
s: South Korea saw a surge of sexually explicit deepfake images and videos made from photos of female classmates, teachers and neighbors and shared in Telegram chat rooms. Many victims were minors and police detained several mostly teenage suspects.

t: Amazon's Alexa Reportedly Shows Political Preference Error in Trump-Harris Presidential Race Queries
s: Amazon's Alexa declined to give reasons to vote for one 2024 presidential candidate but listed reasons to vote for the other, prompting a political backlash. Amazon called it an error and fixed it.

t: Music Producer [name withheld] Reportedly Arrested for Allegedly Using AI-Generated Songs in $10 Million Streaming Scam
s: A US music producer was charged with using hundreds of thousands of AI-generated songs and thousands of bot accounts to fraudulently stream the tracks and collect over $10 million in royalties, while evading streaming platforms' fraud detection. He later pleaded guilty.

t: Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson Soldier Faces Allegations of Using AI to Generate Child Pornography
s: A US Army soldier was charged in federal court with using AI tools and chatbots to create sexual abuse images of real children he knew, built from images taken from social media.

t: Clearview AI Reportedly Faces $33.7 Million Fine for Violating GDPR with Biometric Data Harvesting
s: The Dutch data protection authority fined Clearview AI about 30.5 million euros for building an illegal facial recognition database from billions of photos scraped from the internet without people's consent. Clearview disputes the decision.

t: AI 'Nudify' Apps Used as Tools for Blackmail and Extortion
s: AI 'nudify' apps are being used to create realistic fake nude images of women, which are then used for blackmail, shame and harassment. Victims often have little recourse to get them removed.

t: WiseTech Global CEO [name withheld] Reportedly Deepfaked in Multiple Attempts to Scam Staffers
s: Scammers used AI-generated video of WiseTech Global's CEO in WhatsApp calls to three staff members, asking them for money. The employees recognised the fraud and the attempts failed.

t: Child Predators Are Reportedly Generating Deepfake Nudes of Children to Extort Them
s: A child-protection charity found a dark web manual urging criminals to use AI nudifying tools on images sent by children, then use the altered images to blackmail them into sending more explicit material.

t: ESPN's AI Coverage Reportedly Overlooks [name withheld] in Her Final Match Recap
s: ESPN's AI-generated recap of [name withheld]'s final professional match did not mention her or her retirement, despite the emotional farewell on the field. ESPN later updated the recap.

t: Fraudsters Use Deepfake Video of Tim Cook to Promote Apple Crypto Scam on YouTube
s: A fake live stream on YouTube reused an old interview with Apple's CEO to promote a crypto scam and drew tens of thousands of viewers before being removed.

t: Deepfake ID Sales Allegedly Persist as OnlyFake Reportedly Relaunches with New Fraud Tools
s: OnlyFake, a site selling AI-generated fake ID images, reappeared after an earlier shutdown with new tools such as signature generation. Its documents reportedly bypassed identity checks at banks and crypto exchanges, facilitating fraud and money laundering.

t: Instagram's Algorithm Reportedly Recommended Sexual Content to Teenagers' Accounts
s: Tests by the Wall Street Journal and a researcher found that Instagram Reels recommended sexually suggestive videos to accounts set up as 13-year-olds within minutes, despite Meta's stated restrictions for teens. Meta called the tests unrepresentative.

t: Independent News Sites Flagged as Spam by Facebook's AI Moderation System
s: Facebook flagged ordinary news links from independent publishers in the US and Europe as spam and removed them. Publishers said appeals went unanswered, and some lost traffic.

t: Unrestricted AI Avatar Tool Accidentally Released by TikTok Permits Recitation of Hitler Quotes and Other Harmful Speech
s: TikTok mistakenly released an internal version of its AI avatar tool with no safeguards. A news outlet used it to make avatars read Hitler quotes and tell people to drink bleach, with no AI watermark. TikTok removed it.

t: Google AI Error Prompts Parents to Use Fecal Matter in Child Training Exercise
