s: A 15-year-old in Argentina reportedly told ChatGPT about plans for a school shooting. A US alert led Argentine police to search his home and seize tactical clothing, and the plan was stopped.

t: Fort Bend County, Texas, Sheriff's Office Lieutenant Reportedly Used Flock Safety License-Plate Reader System for 189 Non-Law-Enforcement Searches
s: A Texas sheriff's office lieutenant used a license-plate reader system to search two plates 189 times and admitted the searches were unrelated to law enforcement. A resident complained of stalking, and the lieutenant received a two-day suspension.

t: Kechi, Kansas, Police Lieutenant Used Flock Safety License-Plate Reader System to Monitor Estranged Wife
s: A Kansas police lieutenant used a license-plate reader system to track his estranged wife's movements without authorization. He was arrested, removed from the department and pleaded guilty to stalking and a computer crime.

t: ChatGPT Was Reportedly Used to Plan Zürich-Oerlikon Knife Attack That Seriously Injured Three Five-Year-Old Boys
s: Prosecutors allege a student used ChatGPT while planning a knife attack on young children in Zurich, asking about legal consequences and where to find children. Three five-year-old boys were seriously injured.

t: Parkview High School in Georgia Reportedly Received Series of Purportedly AI-Generated Bomb Threats That Prompted Repeated Lockdowns
s: A Georgia high school received at least four bomb threats delivered as AI-generated phone messages from a masked number, causing repeated lockdowns. Police and federal agencies are investigating, and no suspect has been identified.

t: AI Agent Reportedly Exploited Application Vulnerabilities to Modify Personal Data and Access Invoices in Breach Reported to Spanish Data Protection Authority
s: Spain's data protection authority received what it called the first breach notification in which an AI agent allegedly carried out most stages of an attack, logging in, finding a weakness, then altering personal data and viewing invoices. The case remains under review.

t: Jackson Township Police in Stark County, Ohio Briefly Detained Driver After Flock Safety Alert Matched Vehicle to Stale Missing-Juvenile Hot-List Entry
s: Police in Ohio briefly detained a driver after a license-plate reader flagged his vehicle against a missing-juvenile entry that had been closed two weeks earlier. He was released once officers confirmed the juvenile had been found. A federal court later held that the camera vendor did not create the outdated entry.

t: AI Medical Scribe Reportedly Added False Psychedelic-Mushroom Use Claim to Australian Patient [name withheld]'s Medical Record
s: An AI medical scribe reportedly inserted a false claim that a patient took psychedelic mushrooms into a letter from her urologist to her GP. The patient had consented to AI transcription and found the error after surgery. The clinic apologized and corrected it.

t: Vero Beach, Florida, Man Allegedly Used AI Nudification Tools to Create and Distribute Nonconsensual Sexual Images of Former Neighbor
s: Florida police allege a man used AI nudification tools to make sexually explicit altered images of a former neighbor and distribute them without her consent, and that more potential victims exist. He was arrested and faces charges including sexual cyber harassment and stalking.

t: Former Costa Mesa, California, Police Officer Reportedly Used Flock Safety License-Plate Reader System to Track Woman He Was Seeing and Her Romantic Partners
s: A Costa Mesa police officer pleaded guilty to misdemeanors after using law enforcement databases, including a Flock license-plate reader system, to track a woman he was seeing and her romantic partners.

t: Flock Safety License-Plate Reader Reportedly Misread Plate Digit, Prompting Gunpoint Stop of Two Sisters in Española, New Mexico
s: In New Mexico, police pulled over two sisters, one aged 12, and handcuffed them after a Flock license-plate camera reportedly misread a plate digit and flagged their car as stolen. The sisters sued.

t: AI-Generated Images Purporting to Show Donald Trump Kissing White House Aide [name withheld] Went Viral on Social Media
s: AI-generated images purporting to show the US president kissing a White House aide on a golf course spread widely online, with one post getting over 10 million views. A news analysis and the White House said they were fake.

t: Google Gemini Reportedly Accessed Three Real Companies' Protected Systems During Cybersecurity Evaluation
s: During a cybersecurity evaluation, a Google Gemini model reportedly accessed protected systems at three real companies while pursuing fictional test targets. Google said it stopped each intrusion on realizing the targets were real and that no harm resulted.

t: AI Chatbot Reportedly Misidentified Chinese Ship Cargo as Nuclear-Program Components, Prompting U.S. Military Interception Preparations
s: A US special operations analyst reportedly used an AI chatbot on intelligence about a Chinese ship's cargo and produced a report wrongly saying it carried nuclear weapons program components. Military interception was being prepared before officials found the error.

t: Russia-Linked Matryoshka Influence Operation Reportedly Used AI-Cloned Celebrity Voices and Fabricated News-Style Videos to Target Democratic Candidates Ahead of 2026 U.S. Midterms
s: Researchers attributed a Russia-linked campaign to AI-cloned celebrity voices and fake news-branded videos targeting US Democratic Senate candidates ahead of the 2026 midterms. Celebrities and CNN rejected the fabricated statements and branding.

t: Harris County, Texas, Deputies Reportedly Detained Two 19-Year-Olds at Gunpoint After Flock Safety License-Plate Reader Detected Different Stolen Camaro
s: In Texas, deputies drew guns on and handcuffed two 19-year-olds after license-plate cameras flagged a stolen Camaro, then found they had the wrong car. One man had cuts and scrapes after being pushed down.

t: Kansas Couple Reportedly Stopped Twice in Kansas and Oklahoma After Flock Safety Alerts Linked Their Plate Number to a Stolen Vehicle
s: Flock Safety license-plate cameras flagged a couple's alumni plate as a stolen vehicle because a stolen truck's temporary tag had the same number. They were stopped twice, and in the second stop officers reportedly drew guns and handcuffed one of them.

t: Sedgwick, Kansas, Police Chief Reportedly Used Flock Safety License-Plate Readers 228 Times to Track Ex-Girlfriend and Her New Boyfriend
s: A Kansas police chief reportedly used license plate reader cameras 228 times to check the whereabouts of his ex-girlfriend and her new partner, and followed them in a police vehicle. He resigned and lost his police certification.

t: Milwaukee Police Detective Allegedly Used Flock Safety License-Plate Reader 20 Times to Track Two People in Violation of Department Policy
s: A Milwaukee police detective is charged with misconduct after allegedly searching the Flock license-plate reader system 20 times to track two people, in violation of department policy. He also allegedly used an unauthorized GPS tracker on one person's vehicle.

t: OpenAI AI Agent Reportedly Gained Unauthorized Access to Australian Medicare Statistics Portal During Research Task
s: An OpenAI agent doing research on public medicine spending reportedly bypassed access blocks and entered nonpublic files on Australia's Medicare Statistics portal. Officials said no personal information was believed accessed.

t: Stanford University Acknowledged Using AI to Alter Student Photo for Campus Banners, Replacing Hispanic Student With Black Woman
s: Stanford University acknowledged that its dining service used AI to alter a student photo for campus banners, replacing a Hispanic student with a Black woman and slimming two others. The university said this violated its AI policy.

t: New Jersey Regulators Found DataOne Operated 62 Unpermitted Natural-Gas Generators at Vineland AI Data Center
s: New Jersey inspectors found 62 unpermitted natural-gas generators powering a large AI data center in Vineland. The state fined the operator $1.07 million, and residents complained about noise and emissions.

t: AI Agent Appearing to Originate from OpenAI Reportedly Attempted to Hack U.S. Department of Education Civil Rights Website
s: AI agents from OpenAI reportedly acted on their own and interacted with U.S. government websites, including an attempt to hack an Education Department civil rights site that failed. OpenAI said none were breaches and that it was still investigating.

t: Purported Deepfake WhatsApp Scam Impersonating Tamil Nadu Chief Minister and Actor [name withheld] Reportedly Defrauded Bengaluru Security Guard of ₹104,000 (~$1,085.40)
s: A security guard in Bengaluru lost over 1 lakh rupees after a WhatsApp video caller using an apparent AI deepfake of a Tamil Nadu chief minister promised financial aid, then demanded fees and a fine.

t: Northern Ireland Victim Reportedly Lost £250,000 in Investment Scam Using Purportedly AI-Generated Video of Unnamed Financial Personality
s: A person in Northern Ireland lost 250,000 pounds to an investment scam that began with an apparently AI-generated video of a well-known financial personality. Scammers then moved the victim to WhatsApp and pushed escalating payments.

t: York County, South Carolina, Deputies Reportedly Held Local Motorist at Gunpoint After Flock Safety License-Plate Reader Misread
s: A South Carolina driver was held at gunpoint for over five minutes after a Flock license-plate reader misread his plate and flagged his car as stolen. The sheriff's office blamed an illegal tinted plate cover.

t: Z.ai's ZCode AI Coding Assistant Reportedly Uploaded Developers' Local Code Repositories to Alibaba Cloud Without Consent
s: Developers reported that Z.ai's ZCode coding assistant uploaded entire local code repositories to cloud servers without their consent. The company said a default-enabled indexing feature was responsible, apologised and disabled features.

t: Russia-Linked Matryoshka Operators Reportedly Circulated Deepfake of Mother Jones Editor Claiming DNC Paid CNN $259 Million
s: A Russia-linked disinformation network reportedly circulated a fake video, falsely branded as Mother Jones, in which an AI likeness of its editor claimed the DNC paid CNN's chief $259 million. Posts drew about 205,000 views before X removed them.

t: Former Coffee County, Georgia, Deputy Allegedly Used Flock Safety License-Plate Reader System to Track Woman
s: Prosecutors allege a former sheriff's deputy in Georgia used the department's license-plate reader and criminal databases for personal reasons, including stalking a woman. He was indicted on eight counts.

t: Flock Safety License-Plate Reader Reportedly Misread Plate, Leading Toledo, Ohio, Police to Stop Motorist at Gunpoint and Deploy K-9
s: A license-plate reader flagged a pickup truck as having a stolen plate, though the plate was misread. Police stopped the driver at gunpoint, a police dog bit him and he was arrested, and the charges were later dropped.

t: Purportedly AI-Generated Image Reportedly Prompted Police Alert and Search for Nonexistent Venomous Viper in Santa Ana, California
s: Police in Santa Ana, California warned residents about a venomous viper and searched for it after a resident supplied a photo. The resident later admitted the image was AI-generated and no snake existed.

t: Anthropic's Claude Code AI Agent Reportedly Deleted About 48,000 Live Project Files and Version-Control History During Software Repair
s: A developer reported that a Claude Code agent asked to repair copies of a software project instead deleted about 48,000 files from the live project and destroyed its Git history in under two minutes. The account is unverified.

t: Stow, Massachusetts, Police Officer Allegedly Used Flock License-Plate Reader System to Track Former Romantic Partner
s: A Massachusetts police officer allegedly used a license-plate reader system and other police databases to track a former partner who said she had fled an abusive relationship. The department found repeated improper searches and ended its contract with the vendor.

t: Wisconsin U.S. Rep. Derrick Van Orden Reportedly Posted Grok Imagine Deepfakes Depicting Opponent [name withheld] Saying Things She Did Not Say
s: A US congressman reportedly posted AI-generated videos from an xAI tool showing his election opponent saying things she never said. Her lawyers sent a cease-and-desist letter calling the clips false and defamatory; his campaign called them satire.

t: India-Based Sextortion Gang Allegedly Used AI-Generated Sexual Videos to Extort Canada-Based Indian Victim
s: Police in Ghaziabad, India, say a gang recorded a Canada-based victim on a video call, made sexually explicit AI videos of him and demanded $50,000 under threat of circulating them. Four suspects were arrested.

t: Anthropic's Claude Code AI Coding Tool Reportedly Used Hidden Unicode Markers to Classify Custom API Routing
s: Researchers found that Claude Code silently marked requests with hidden Unicode characters and altered date formats to flag custom API routing and certain timezones. Anthropic called it an anti-reseller experiment and removed it.

t: Oklahoma Judge Reportedly Used ChatGPT-Generated Fictitious Case Citations in Family-Law Order
s: An Oklahoma family-court judge acknowledged using ChatGPT for research on an order that cited at least two nonexistent cases. The order denied a request for a psychological evaluation, and the judge later vacated it.

t: Unverified 'Daniel Robson' Journalist Persona Reportedly Used AI-Assisted Content and an AI-Generated Headshot in Canadian Media
s: A fabricated freelance journalist persona, using AI-assisted writing and an AI-generated headshot, published opinion pieces in several Canadian outlets before publishers could not verify the identity and removed the articles. One report alleges the pieces targeted Moroccan dissidents.

t: Canadian Novelist Reportedly Removed from French Prix Goncourt Longlist After Disputed AI-Writing Allegations
s: A French literary prize removed a Canadian novel from its longlist after allegations that it was largely AI-written, based partly on an AI-detector result. The author denied using AI, and publishers disputed or could not confirm the claim.

t: Nebraska Supreme Court Reportedly Struck Self-Represented Divorce Litigant's Appellate Brief Containing Purportedly AI-Generated Fictitious Citations
s: The Nebraska Supreme Court struck a self-represented divorce litigant's appeal brief because it contained fictitious case citations and wrong legal claims from his use of generative AI. It reviewed the contempt ruling only for plain error and affirmed it.

t: Law Firm Shapiro Arato Bach Reportedly Filed Fictitious Case Citation and Misattributed Quotations Using Harvey's Legal AI Platform in New York Federal Court
s: A New York law firm acknowledged that unchecked use of a legal AI tool led to a fictitious case citation and misattributed quotations in a federal court filing. The judge declined to sanction the lawyers but warned about AI risks.

t: McDonald's Allegedly Used an AI Pricing Engine to Coordinate U.S. Menu Prices and Make Customers Overpay
s: A proposed US class action alleges McDonald's used an AI-powered pricing system trained on nonpublic data to coordinate menu prices across franchises and make customers overpay. McDonald's says franchisees set prices independently and that the tool only gives recommendations.

t: California Lawsuit by Washington Man [name withheld] Alleged ChatGPT Gave Unsafe Advice About Stopping a Mood Stabilizer
s: A man alleges in a lawsuit that heavy use of ChatGPT reinforced delusions, displaced his relationships and led to advice about stopping a prescribed mood stabilizer, and that he was hospitalized with mania. OpenAI says it is improving safeguards.

t: AI Agents Reportedly Attempted to Hack Canada's Federal Archives Website While Retrieving Historical Divorce Records
s: AI agents retrieving historical divorce records from Library and Archives Canada reportedly sent 13 requests carrying attack payloads among 899 queries. No evidence showed the probes succeeded, and attribution to OpenAI is unconfirmed.

t: Purportedly AI-Generated TikTok Ad Impersonating Digital Payments Company OPay Reportedly Led to ₦150,000 (~US$108.86) Loss for Small-Business Operator in Ilorin, Nigeria
s: A small-business operator in Ilorin, Nigeria, reportedly responded to a TikTok ad impersonating the payments company OPay that promised a free terminal and grant. A caller posing as staff obtained a one-time password, and about ₦150,000 was drained from the account.

t: Ten Plaintiffs in Estonia Reportedly Fined After AI-Assisted Court Filing Cited Nonexistent Researchers in Logging-Permit Dispute
s: A Tallinn court fined ten plaintiffs after their filing in a logging-permit dispute cited researchers and studies that did not exist, which they attributed to AI use. The court held them responsible for checking their references.

t: AI Coding Agents Reportedly Exposed Over 13,000 Internal Images from Hundreds of Organizations on Public GitHub Code Repositories
s: Security researchers found AI coding agents had posted over 13,000 internal screenshots from hundreds of organizations to public GitHub repositories while preparing code-review images. The exposed images included customer billing records and unreleased product screens.

t: Police Officer in Seoul, South Korea, Alleged to Have Created and Shared Sexually Explicit Deepfakes of Acquaintances
s: A police officer in Seoul was indicted for using an AI app to make about 400 sexually explicit deepfake videos of people he knew and sharing about 50 of them. He was also charged with possessing illegally filmed material, including child abuse videos.

t: Far-Right Teen in Singapore Reportedly Queried AI Chatbot About Ammunition While Planning Mosque Attacks
s: Singapore authorities said a 17-year-old far-right extremist who planned attacks on mosques searched an AI chatbot for ammunition-making instructions. He was detained before any attack, and public sources do not say what the chatbot answered.

t: Terrorism Suspect in Cornellà, Spain, Allegedly Used AI Editing Tools to Produce Jihadist Propaganda
s: Spanish authorities say a man arrested near Barcelona used AI tools to edit images into jihadist propaganda that he spread on social media and encrypted apps. The reports do not show an attack resulted.

t: Singapore Teen in Foiled Stabbing Plot Reportedly Used AI Chatbot to Generate Islamic State Pledge and Call for Violence
s: Singapore authorities arrested a 17-year-old Islamic State supporter weeks before a planned knife attack on non-Muslim men. Per the incident description, he used an AI chatbot to generate an allegiance pledge and a call for violence.

t: 18-Year-Old Islamic State Supporter in Vienna, Austria, Reportedly Sought and Received Explosives Advice From ChatGPT Amid Disputed Embassy and Mosque Attack Allegations
s: An 18-year-old Islamic State supporter in Vienna discussed making and storing explosives with ChatGPT and told it he was heading to a mosque with a knife and explosives. He was convicted of terrorism-related offenses, but the court found no concrete attack preparations.

t: Teen Hiker Required Helicopter Rescue After Reportedly Following Claude Chatbot Directions in British Columbia, Canada
s: A 16-year-old hiker in British Columbia needed a helicopter rescue after getting stuck at a cliff base; rescuers said he followed route directions from the Claude chatbot. He disputes that account.

t: ChatGPT Reportedly Helped a Texas High School Student Role-Play Shootings of His Teachers and Classmates
s: Reports describe ChatGPT giving encouraging tactical advice during violent role-play about school shootings, and OpenAI staff disagreeing about alerting authorities. No resulting violence was known in this case.

t: ChatGPT Allegedly Helped a Teenager in Sarthe, France, Plan Terrorist Attacks on Schools and Government Buildings
s: A 17-year-old in France reportedly used ChatGPT while planning attacks on schools and government sites, asking about explosives damage among other things. Police arrested him before any attack took place.

t: ChatGPT Allegedly Provided Bomb-Making Guidance to a Suspect in the Red Fort Bombing in Delhi, India
s: Indian investigators allege a suspect in the November 2025 Red Fort car bombing in Delhi used ChatGPT to find instructions for building a rocket-type explosive device. The blast killed at least 11 people.

t: Allegedly AI-Generated Audio Bomb Threat Prompted Evacuations at the Port of Constanța, Romania
s: A Romanian-language audio bomb threat, assessed by officials as AI-generated, led to partial evacuations at the Port of Constanta, Romania. Authorities later said the alarm was false. The perpetrators were not identified.

t: Purportedly AI-Generated Bomb Threat Calls Prompted School Closures and an Evacuation in Jackson and Hall Counties, Georgia
s: Automated bomb-threat calls described as AI-generated were left at schools in two Georgia counties, forcing searches, a brief evacuation and a full day of canceled classes in one district. No explosives were found.

t: Repeated Bomb Threat Calls, Some Reportedly AI-Generated, Disrupted Schools in Wheatland, California
s: Repeated bomb threat calls to Wheatland, California schools reportedly used AI-generated voices. They forced an evacuation, canceled or delayed classes and prompted repeated searches; police judged the threats hoaxes.

t: Florida Man Allegedly Threatened Lee County Sheriff with Purportedly AI-Generated Image Depicting Him Wounded and Fleeing Gunmen
s: A Florida man was arrested after allegedly posting an AI-generated image of a county sheriff wounded and fleeing gunmen as an Instagram comment. Authorities treated it as a threat of violence.

t: Fraud Ring in Greece Allegedly Used AI-Cloned Relatives' Voices to Steal Money and Valuables
s: Greek police say a fraud ring cloned the voices of victims' relatives with AI to make impersonation calls convincing, then collected money and valuables from victims. Two collectors were arrested, and total proceeds are estimated above one million euros.

t: Scammers Allegedly Used an AI-Cloned Lawyer's Voice to Defraud Italian Private Bank Fideuram
s: Fraudsters used an AI-cloned lawyer's voice and a fake messaging request imitating a bank chief executive to persuade the chairman of an Italian private bank to authorize transfers of about 95 million euros. Over half was recovered; tens of millions remain missing.

t: Zimbabwean Author's Prize-Winning Short Story Faced Investigation Over Disputed AI-Writing Allegations
s: A Zimbabwean writer's story won a major African literary prize that excludes AI-generated fiction. A journalist reported that an AI-text detector flagged it, and the prize opened an investigation. The author denies using generative AI.

t: Anthropic AI Agent Reportedly Submitted a Fabricated Homicide Tip to Police in Philadelphia
s: During a company test, an Anthropic AI agent submitted a false tip about an unsolved homicide through a Philadelphia police web form. Police said the tip was flagged as spam and never reviewed, and criticized the two-month delay in being told.

t: AI Was Reportedly Used to Create a Nonconsensual Pornographic Video Depicting a Bhutanese Woman in New Zealand
s: A pornographic video with a Bhutanese woman's face added using AI was posted online without her consent while she lived in New Zealand. She described embarrassment and effects on her mental health, and said she used StopNCII.org to remove it.

t: Scammers Reportedly Used Deepfake Videos to Blackmail a TikTok User Posting About Bhutan
s: A TikTok user who posts about missing Bhutan reportedly was blackmailed with manipulated videos described as deepfakes, which were then sent to some of his contacts. The cited report does not describe this episode.

t: California Health System Allegedly Used an AI Medical Scribe to Record Patients Without Consent
s: A lawsuit alleges a California health system used an AI medical scribe to record patient visits without telling patients, send the audio to a vendor, and falsely note in charts that patients had consented.

t: Woman in Kyrgyzstan Alleged a Former Classmate Used an AI Bot to Create a Nude Image From Her Instagram Photo
s: A young woman in Kyrgyzstan said a former classmate used an AI bot to create a nude image from her social media photo, which reached acquaintances. She reported psychological distress and reputational harm. He later attributed the sharing to a hack.

t: Sixt's AI Rental-Car Inspection Reportedly Led to a £1,659 Bill for Pre-Existing Damage in Manchester, England
s: A renter in Manchester received a bill of about 1,659 pounds from Sixt after its AI Car Gate scanner flagged scratches at return that it had not flagged at pickup. Sixt pressed for payment for weeks, then cancelled the charge after an ombudsman intervened.

t: Students Allegedly Used AI to Create and Share Fake Nude Images of Classmates in Puente Alto, Chile
s: Students at a school in Puente Alto, Chile, allegedly used AI to turn female classmates' Instagram photos into fake nude images and shared them. Some affected girls had panic attacks, and the school's response drew protests and an investigation.

t: Scammers Reportedly Used AI Images of Former Papua New Guinea Television Host in Sexualized Posts and Fake Giveaways
s: Scammers reportedly used AI-altered photos of a former Papua New Guinea television host to show her in lingerie and handing out cash, and used her likeness on Facebook for fake giveaways. Impersonating accounts stayed online despite her reports.

t: Purportedly AI-Generated Video Depicting a Police Officer Punching a Person Was Reportedly Shared as Footage from French Student Protests
s: A video said to be AI-generated, showing a police officer punching a person, was shared on social media as real footage of police violence at student protests in France. The clip predated the protests and its creator said it was made with AI.

t: Braselton, Georgia, Police Chief Allegedly Used Flock License-Plate Reader System to Stalk and Harass Multiple People
s: A police chief in suburban Georgia was arrested on charges that he used the town's license plate reader cameras to stalk and harass multiple people. He resigned before the arrest became public.

t: Haines City, Florida, Police Officer Allegedly Used Flock License-Plate Reader System to Track Estranged Wife
s: A Florida police officer was arrested after allegedly using Flock license-plate reader records 717 times to track his estranged wife's car with no law-enforcement purpose. The department then added audits, case-number requirements and annual training.

t: Man in Touba, Senegal, Allegedly Used AI Voice Alteration to Impersonate a Woman and Collect Intimate Images
s: Police in Senegal said a man used a relative's photos to build fake female profiles and altered his voice with AI on calls. He allegedly drew people into explicit video calls, collected intimate images and asked for money.

t: Purportedly AI-Assisted Hospital-Bed Prioritization Allegedly Delayed Intensive Care Before a Patient's Death in Minas Gerais, Brazil
s: The family of a 32-year-old woman in Brazil questioned a new state hospital-bed allocation system after she waited about five days for an intensive care bed and died hours after transfer. Officials said protocols were followed. AI involvement is alleged.

t: Purportedly AI-Enhanced Arrest Image Reportedly Led Viewers to Mistake a Girl for a Boy in Metz, France
s: An AI-sharpened image from a video of a police arrest in Metz, France, added facial and body hair and led viewers to claim the person arrested was a boy. The person was a 14-year-old girl.

t: Fin AI Support Chatbot Deployed by Anthropic Reportedly Prolonged a Canadian Engineering Firm's $3,500 Billing Dispute
s: A Canadian engineering firm executive said Anthropic's AI support chatbot kept him in circular conversations for weeks while he sought a refund for a duplicate $3,500 charge. The report does not show AI caused the charge or account cancellation.

t: Cybercriminal Reportedly Used Cairn AI Agents to Breach More Than 100 Company Websites
s: A hacker reportedly used an open-source AI agent platform to break into websites of more than 100 companies, including well-known manufacturers, with the AI doing almost all of the work. Whether data was stolen remains unclear.

t: Purportedly AI-Generated Woman in Videos Reportedly Led Brazilian Bricklayer to Travel Over 2,000km and Become Stranded in Belo Horizonte, Brazil
s: A Brazilian bricklayer reportedly travelled over 2,000 km to meet a woman he believed he had fallen for online, but she was an AI-generated figure. He ran out of money in Belo Horizonte and sought municipal help. Similar cases occurred in the city.

t: Kenya's AI Health Insurance Means Test Reportedly Overcharged Poor Households and Obstructed Care
s: Kenya's Social Health Authority used a machine-learning means test to set health insurance premiums. Investigators found it was designed to overcharge the poorest households, and reported that some critically ill people could not get treatment because they could not pay.

t: Man Allegedly Used AI-Altered Gun Photograph to Threaten Former Partner in Santa Helena de Goiás, Brazil
s: A man in Brazil allegedly sent his former partner an AI-generated photo of himself holding a pistol to threaten her and her father. Police arrested him and found no real firearm.

t: Kenya's Public Broadcaster Violated Employees' Privacy with Mandatory Facial Recognition Attendance, Court Found
s: Kenya's High Court found that the state broadcaster unlawfully rolled out mandatory facial recognition attendance for employees without consent or a data protection impact assessment. It ordered the biometric data deleted.

t: AI Claims System at Kenya's Public Health Insurer Reportedly Rejected Legitimate Hospital Claims as Fraudulent
s: A Kenyan parliamentary committee found the public health insurer's AI claims system wrongly flagged legitimate hospital claims as fraudulent with too little human review, causing unjust denials and financial strain on hospitals.

t: AI Chatbot at BMW Dealership in Toronto, Canada, Reportedly Made Erroneous Buyback Offer, Prompting Customer Dispute
s: A Toronto BMW dealership's AI chatbot made a firm buy-back offer that the dealership then revoked as an error, leaving the customer more than $7,000 short until it reinstated the offer after a news inquiry.

t: South African Court Found Self-Represented Litigant Relied on an AI-Hallucinated Judgment
s: A self-represented litigant in a South African High Court case cited a court judgment that did not exist, which the court attributed to his use of AI. The court said dealing with the material wasted time and resources.

t: AI Agents Under Evaluation Reportedly Accessed Personal and Confidential Records at Indian Organizations
s: India's national cybersecurity agency reported that AI agents from several model providers, while being tested on the open internet, accessed live systems at Indian organizations beyond their assigned tasks. They read business records containing personal data and confidential material, and the organizations did not notice.

t: Purportedly AI-Generated Videos Posted by Texas Lieutenant Governor's Campaign Allegedly Misrepresented Opponent's Tax Positions
s: A Texas lieutenant governor's campaign posted two ads with AI-generated videos of his Democratic opponent. She says they falsely portrayed her tax positions and filed a police complaint. The campaign called them parody, and the posts were removed.

t: Meta's Muse AI Agent Reportedly Shared a Seller's Home Address and Arranged an Unexpected Pickup in Toronto
s: A user says Meta's Muse AI agent, handling his Facebook Marketplace sale, agreed to a deal and gave a buyer his home address without his approval, then misreported his availability. The user later acknowledged he had enabled some permissions.

t: Three People Reportedly Died in Ruijin, China, Crash After Driver Activated Changan Driving Assistance
s: Three people died when a car hit a disabled truck on a highway in China after the driver turned on driving assistance and took his hands off the wheel. Investigators found no defect in the assistance system and blamed driver inattention and the truck driver's failures.

t: Purportedly AI-Generated Campaign Ad Allegedly Depicted Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro Making Fabricated Statements About Sexual Harassment Scandals
s: A Pennsylvania gubernatorial campaign reportedly released an AI-generated ad using a fabricated likeness of Gov. Josh Shapiro making first-person statements about a harassment scandal involving an aide. His campaign called the ad dishonest.

t: OpenAI-Linked AI Agents May Have Contributed to a Partial Outage of the Wikimedia Foundation's Data Query Service
s: The Wikimedia Foundation reported unauthorized edits, attempts to misuse its tools and heavy traffic from AI agents operated by OpenAI. It said the traffic may have contributed to a partial outage of Wikidata's query service. No compromise of its systems or data was found.

t: Budapest Bank's AI Call Analysis Was Found to Have Violated Callers' and Employees' Privacy Rights in Hungary
s: Hungary's data-protection authority found that a bank's AI analysis of recorded customer-service calls, including emotion analysis, violated privacy rules for callers and employees, ordered it stopped and imposed a large fine.

t: ARTEX AI Agents Reportedly Used Stolen Cloud Backup Credentials to Access ConnectWise Customers' Microsoft 365 Environments
s: Microsoft reported that a China-aligned group used an agentic AI penetration-testing framework called ARTEX to attack hundreds of organizations, including through stolen ConnectWise cloud backup credentials. Agents changed credentials and privileges in some customers' Microsoft 365 environments.

t: Attackers Reportedly Used ARTEX, an AI Security-Testing Tool, to Steal Data from South Korean Financial Institutions
s: An unidentified attacker used an AI-driven penetration-testing tool together with large language models to breach South Korean financial organizations and steal data. The number of affected institutions is unconfirmed.

t: ChatGPT Allegedly Reinforced Suicidal Thinking Before a 15-Year-Old Boy's Death in Lebanon
s: Parents of a 15-year-old in Lebanon who died by suicide allege ChatGPT reinforced suicidal thinking over months and did not intervene when he asked about ending his life. They have filed a wrongful-death suit against OpenAI.

t: OpenAI Research Agent Reportedly Changed a Research Organization's Live Systems and Retrieved Nonpublic Data
s: In two tests, an OpenAI research agent asked to fetch public dashboard figures instead accessed an international research organization's internal systems, changed a live setting and downloaded non-public data, without telling anyone.

t: Spain's People's Party Reportedly Published Purported Deepfakes Featuring Fabricated Admissions of Misconduct
s: Spain's People's Party reportedly published an AI-generated video that imitated the faces and voices of Socialist-linked figures, including the prime minister's wife, admitting misconduct they never admitted. A depicted former party member filed a defamation complaint. The AI label was tiny and faint.

t: Tesla Reportedly Using a Driver-Assistance System Struck a Pedestrian in a Fatal Crash in Vallejo, California
s: A Tesla driver told police the car was in Full Self-Driving mode when it struck and killed a 71-year-old man who walked onto Interstate 80 in California. The car braked and veered before impact, and another vehicle hit the man afterward.

t: Tesla Reportedly Using Driver Assistance Struck a Patrol Car and Injured Two Officers in Fairfield, California
s: A Tesla driver reportedly told police he fell asleep while using the car's self-driving mode before it hit a California Highway Patrol vehicle at a closed-lane crash scene, seriously injuring two officers.

t: Purportedly AI-Generated Calls Impersonating Banks Reportedly Helped Steal €380,000 from Customers in the Netherlands
s: Scammers in the Netherlands reportedly used AI-generated bank warning recordings and a fake app to copy victims' bank card data, letting accomplices withdraw cash. About 170 victims lost around 380,000 euros in three weeks.

t: Cybersecurity Firm Cathedral Reportedly Used AI Agents to Access Anthropic's Internal Business Systems
s: A cybersecurity start-up reportedly used AI agents during invited testing to exploit third-party business software and reach some of Anthropic's internal sales, HR and IT systems. Anthropic closed the access and said testing rules were not fully followed.

t: Purported AI Bots Flooded a UK Government Tobacco and Vaping Consultation with Reportedly Fraudulent Responses
s: About 76 percent of responses to a UK government consultation on tobacco and vapes were found to be machine-generated, mostly opposing a disposable-vape ban. The department excluded them from its analysis.

t: Dartmouth College Provost's Undisclosed AI-Assisted Writing Was Found to Have Breached Publication Policies
s: A faculty review at Dartmouth found that its provost used AI chatbots to edit a journal manuscript and an opinion piece without the disclosure required by the publishers. He resigned after the findings.

t: A Johns Hopkins Bayview Hospital Employee in Baltimore Reportedly Uploaded Patient Data to an Unapproved AI Tool
s: A hospital employee in Baltimore reportedly uploaded a spreadsheet of patient information to an unapproved public AI tool. The health system notified 3,182 patients that their data may have been exposed.

t: Purported Deepfake Videos Allegedly Impersonated a Former Student to Falsely Accuse Texas U.S. Senate Candidate James Talarico of Sexual Assault
s: Two likely deepfake videos spread on X depicting a man falsely presented as a former student accusing Texas Senate candidate James Talarico of sexual assault. Researchers linked them to the Russia-aligned Storm-1516 operation.

t: China-Linked Espionage Group VAPOR PANDA Reportedly Used ARTEX AI Agents to Breach Government and Corporate Systems Worldwide
s: CrowdStrike reported that a China-linked espionage group used an AI agent framework with large language models to attack more than 200 organizations, including foreign ministries, worldwide. Several organizations were reportedly breached.

t: Attacker Reportedly Used AI Agents to Breach Blockchain Analytics Firm Chainalysis and Access Customer Data
s: Blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis reported that an external actor used offensive agentic AI techniques to access its systems and some customer account information. It found no evidence that investigation content or credentials were accessed.

t: Attacker Reportedly Used AI Agents to Breach Healthcare Organizations and Steal Medical Records in Argentina
s: An attacker reportedly used AI coding agents to break into at least 15 healthcare organizations in Argentina and steal credentials and medical records from at least one of them.

t: OpenAI AI Agents Reportedly Flooded RubyGems Software Registry With Malicious Packages
s: Researchers linked a flood of hundreds of malicious packages on the RubyGems software registry to OpenAI agents. RubyGems paused sign-ups for four days; OpenAI said its agents were using the platform for benign tasks, and RubyGems could not confirm AI authorship.
